The script generates a set of 1500 randomly distributed points within a predefined BC-Albers coordinate bounding box (EPSG:3005), computes a full distance matrix between all point pairs, and constructs Voronoi polygons from those points — producing vector geometry outputs (memory layers) for spatial pattern analysis, tessellation, or proximity modeling. No raster or time-series data is used; the workflow is purely vector-based geometric processing using QGIS native algorithms.

Summarize population by administrative boundary. The script loads an Ethiopia administrative shapefile (EAS.shp) and a WorldPop 2020 raster (eth_ppp_2020_UNadj_constrained.tif), filters features to 'Tahtay Adiyabo' admin3 units (and optionally by population sum outside 2000–3500), fixes geometries, computes zonal sum statistics of population values per polygon, then sorts and prints results by vertex count with formatted population sums and GAT IDs.

Compare administrative unit population estimates. The script compares population estimates from a raster dataset (MetaFocus_v1.tif) against existing polygon-level population values (Met_Pop) in an Ethiopia administrative shapefile (eth_verification_gat_v2.shp). It loads and fixes the vector layer, optionally filters by administrative name ('Tahtay Adiyabo'), overlays it with the raster using zonal statistics (sum), computes geometric metrics (centroid, area in km², Polsby-Popper compactness index, bounding box height), and outputs a sorted tabular summary showing vertex count, bounding box height, original vs. raster-derived population, feature ID, area, and compactness — flagged with ↑/↓ indicators when outside user-defined thresholds (2000–3500). Summary counts report how many units fall below, within, or above the threshold range.

Calculate area-weighted average perimeter. The script computes the area-weighted average perimeter (AwaP) of building blocks (polygonal urban fabric features) intersecting or contained within a user-defined boundary. It first preprocesses input vector layers (fixing geometries, reprojecting, dissolving touching polygons, removing holes), optionally applies a morphological buffering 'dead-end removal' operation to smooth block outlines, then selects qualifying blocks based on spatial predicates (intersects, within, or percent-in-boundary threshold), computes each block’s perimeter and area, and finally calculates AwaP = Σ(Perimeter × Area) / Σ(Area). Output is a memory vector layer named 'AwaP_X' (where X is the computed value in meters), visualized in QGIS with a custom red color, and the scalar AwaP result is displayed in the plugin dialog label (e.g., '124.3 m').

Map ecological connectivity opportunities. The script processes a set of preloaded QGIS vector and raster layers—representing habitat types (woodland, wetland, grassland), ecological networks, erosion risk, water regulation opportunities, restoration ease, and multi-benefit areas—against a grid-based zone file (grids.geojson). For each grid cell (identified by unique 'id'), it extracts: (1) vector-derived categorical attributes (e.g., 'Core', 'Catchment', 'Legend') from overlapping features, normalized via string cleaning (removing punctuation, lowercasing, underscore substitution); and (2) raster-derived normalized min/max statistics (0–1 range) from continuous rasters (e.g., water runoff moderation, ecological network resistance, precipitation erosion risk), using zonal statistics after masking nodata and polygonizing valid data areas. The final output is a GeoJSON (gridsout.geojson) where each grid feature’s properties include a nested 'legends' object aggregating per-map vector lists and ramp-normalized min/max values per grid ID.

Assess ecological network connectivity. The script processes QGIS vector and raster layers to compute per-grid (5 km WGS84 grid) summaries of ecosystem service indicators. For vector layers, it extracts attribute values (e.g., 'Catchmnt', 'Core', 'Legend') or layer presence intersecting each grid cell, deduplicates and normalizes strings via regex-based formatting. For raster layers, it computes zonal min/max statistics over data-covered areas (after nodata masking and polygonization), then normalizes those values to [0,1] using user-provided or auto-derived global min/max, optionally applying custom stop-based interpolation or inversion. Outputs are embedded as nested 'legends' objects in a GeoJSON grid file, structured by thematic map group (e.g., 'moderate_surface_water_runoff', 'woodland_ecosystem'), with vector results as string lists and ramp results as {'min': x, 'max': y} per grid ID. The study uses pre-loaded QGIS layers — no GEE server-side computation occurs; this is a QGIS Python Processing script, not a Google Earth Engine script — and relies on local files ('wgs84_5k_grid.geojson') and a QGIS project with a layer group named 'English'. Data sources are internal to the QGIS project and not programmatically loaded from remote repositories or Earth Engine assets.

Extract glacier outline from NetCDF mask. The script loads a user-selected NetCDF file and a specified variable (e.g., a binary glacier mask), polygonizes it to create vector polygons, filters for glacier pixels (DN = 1), converts those polygons to lines, isolates closed-loop line features (i.e., glacier perimeter contours), sorts them by length, selects the second longest closed loop (intended as the primary glacier outline, excluding outer domain or artifact loops), saves it as a new line layer, extracts its vertices as point features, and exports the vertex coordinates (X,Y) to a CSV file. Outputs include: (1) raster layer of the NetCDF variable, (2) polygonized vector layer, (3) line layer of glacier boundaries, (4) memory layer containing only the second longest closed loop, (5) point layer of its vertices, and (6) CSV file listing all vertex coordinates.

Calculate catchment area from points. The script calculates the upslope (contributing) catchment area for each point feature in an input vector layer using a digital elevation model (DEM). It iterates over each point, uses SAGA's 'upslopearea' algorithm to generate a raster catchment mask where cells draining to the point are assigned value 100, then polygonizes that raster and exports only the DN=100 polygons as individual ESRI Shapefiles (one per point) into a user-specified output folder. The workflow relies entirely on local QGIS processing algorithms ('saga:upslopearea' and 'gdal:polygonize') and does not use Earth Engine APIs or remote sensing imagery processing.

Calculate stage-volume curve from DTM. The script computes a stage-volume relationship from a digital terrain model (DTM) by iterating elevation levels from the minimum to the maximum in 10 increments. It uses QGIS's raster surface volume tool to calculate the volume below each level, converts volumes from cubic meters to cubic kilometers, and merges the results into a single vector layer containing elevation level and absolute volume for each stage.

Compute stage-volume curve. The script computes the stage-volume relationship from a DEM by calculating surface volume at multiple water levels derived from the elevation range, producing a merged table with level and absolute volume in cubic kilometers.

Extract forest stand data by perimeter. The script extracts forest stand vector and raster datasets from the TBk (Bestandeskarte) inventory dataset using a user-defined extraction perimeter (a GeoPackage polygon layer). It first filters the main stand layer (TBk_Bestandeskarte.shp) by spatial intersection with the perimeter, then creates two buffered/dissolved versions of the extracted stands: a tightly buffered (0.0001°) version for vector-layer clipping (using 'are within' predicate), and a coarsely buffered (10 m) version for raster clipping (using GDAL's cliprasterbymasklayer). All listed vector datasets (e.g., TBk_local_densities.gpkg, stands_simplified.shp) and raster datasets (e.g., dg_layer.tif, VHM_10m.tif, classified_smooth_2.tif) are clipped to their respective buffered perimeters. Outputs include the filtered stand layer and all clipped vector/raster layers written to the specified output directory.

Extract forest stand perimeters and associated raster/vector layers. The script extracts forest stand polygons (TBk_Bestandeskarte), local density vector features, and a 10m canopy height model (VHM) raster clipped to a buffered and dissolved extraction perimeter. It first builds spatial indexes on input vector layers, then extracts TBk_Bestandeskarte features intersecting the user-provided 'Extraction Perimeter', buffers and dissolves those stands twice — once with a user-defined buffer (default 10 m) for raster clipping and once with a tiny buffer (0.0001) for vector containment filtering — then clips the 'vhm_10m' raster using the larger buffered polygon and extracts 'local_densities' features that are fully within the tiny-buffered polygon. Outputs are three geospatial products: a clipped VHM raster ('vhm_10m_extracted'), an extracted TBk stand vector layer ('TBk_Bestandeskarte_extracted'), and an extracted local densities vector layer ('local_densities_extracted').

Delineate forest stand classes. The script generates a forest stand delineation (BK) raster-to-vector workflow using a Vegetation Height Model (VHM) at 1m resolution. It applies a multi-step classification: (1) reclassifies VHM into six height-based forest development stages (Ju, SH1–SH2, BH1–BH2) using user-defined upper limits (e.g., LIMIT_JU=7 m); (2) performs two focal statistics passes — first over SH1-inclusive cells (window size=5, 40% majority threshold), then over all cells (window size=25, majority); (3) converts the final smoothed raster to polygons; (4) simplifies geometry (simplify_threshold=2); (5) merges polygons smaller than min_area_bk=2000 m² with neighbors; and (6) clips and dissolves outputs by a user-provided perimeter shapefile (dissolved on field 'Eigentue_1' by default), optionally split and cleaned using forest roads. Outputs include a final merged and attribute-filtered shapefile ('bk_final.shp'), intermediate rasters and vectors in timestamped subfolders, and a processing log.

Reclassify and focal process VHM rasters. The script processes Vegetation Height Model (VHM) rasters by (1) clipping them to individual polygon features (identified by 'id' attribute in perimeter_dissolve), (2) reclassifying pixel values using a lookup table (e.g., mapping original classes to new integer codes), (3) applying focal statistics (majority or SH1-weighted classification) over a user-defined window radius, and (4) converting the final reclassified/focal rasters to vector polygons. Outputs include clipped TIFFs, reclassified TIFFs, focal-processed TIFFs, and polygonized shapefiles — all named per feature ID (e.g., 'vhm_1.tif', 'vhm_recl_1.tif', 'vhm_focal_1.tif', 'vhm_poly_1.shp').

Calculate coniferous proportion per stand. The script calculates the mean coniferous proportion for each forest stand by applying zonal statistics (mean) from a coniferous raster to a vector stands layer, adding an NH field. If calc_main_layer is True, it processes a canopy cover raster: resamples to 1m, aggregates sum per 10m grid cells, thresholds at 40% cover to create a mask, multiplies with the coniferous raster, and computes zonal statistics to generate NH_OS and NH_OS_PIX fields, removing temporary fields and intermediate rasters.

Clip stands and eliminate gaps. This script clips forest stand polygons to an exact perimeter boundary and removes small gaps by merging them with neighboring stands using QGIS processing tools. It first clips the merged stand layer and a tree highest point layer to the perimeter. It then identifies gaps via difference and union operations, merges selected polygons with eliminate, and deletes remaining unprocessed gaps. Optionally, it clips a VHM raster to the perimeter using gdal:cliprasterbymasklayer. Outputs include the clipped stands shapefile and the clipped raster.

Detect forest stand upper layer change. The script computes two raster outputs: (1) 'change_DG' — a byte raster encoding four states of upper-layer presence/absence change between old and new TBk versions using the formula '(A*10 + B) + 1', where A is old DG (0 or 10) and B is new DG (0 or 1); resulting values are 1 (no upper layer in both), 2 (gain), 11 (loss), 12 (maintain); (2) 'change_DG_hdom' — a byte raster extending change detection to identify cleared areas in stands with hdom_old ≥ thresh_hdom (default 25 m) where hdom reduction exceeds thresh_hdiff (default 7 m), encoded as value 100; all other pixels retain original change_DG codes or are zeroed if hdom_old < threshold. Inputs are vector stand boundaries (with 'hdom' attribute) and co-registered DG rasters for old and new TBk versions.

Clean forest stand geometry. The script cleans a forest stand map (TBk Bestandeskarte) by removing features with area < 100 m² and null area values, fixing invalid geometries, dropping the original 'ID' field, and replacing it with a new auto-incremented 'ID' field. All operations are performed using QGIS native processing algorithms within a PyQGIS processing model; no Earth Engine (GEE) code is present—the script is purely a QGIS Processing Algorithm.

Extract TBk project data by perimeter. This QGIS script extracts all polygons from a TBk (Toolkit Bestandeskarte) forest stand map that intersect a user-defined perimeter polygon. It also selectively extracts associated raster and vector layers (degree of cover rasters, vegetation height models, coniferous rasters, intermediate processing layers, local densities, and additional user-specified materials). The algorithm uses 'extract by location' for vector layers and 'clip raster by mask layer' (or extent) for rasters. Outputs preserve the original folder structure and file naming.

Compute hdom deviation from VHM. The script computes the difference raster 'diff_hdom_vhm' by subtracting a rasterized stand-level hdom (height dominant) attribute — derived from the vector layer 'tbk_bestandesgrenzen' (forest stand boundaries) — from the input VHM_10m (vegetation height model at 10 m resolution). It also generates a point layer 'vhm_10m_points' by converting each pixel of the VHM_10m raster to a point with its value. The workflow uses GDAL rasterize (with hdom field, 10 m resolution, Float32), GDAL raster calculator (B − A, where B is VHM_10m and A is rasterized hdom), and QGIS native pixel-to-points conversion.

Merge forest stand maps with unique IDs. This QGIS processing algorithm merges multiple TBk forest stand map vector layers into one. It first sorts the layers spatially (northernmost first, then westernmost) using bounding box coordinates. It renames the original 'ID' field to 'ID_pre_merge', then adds two new fields: 'ID_meta' containing a unique prefix (alphabetical A, B, C... or numerical 1, 2, 3...) for each layer, and 'ID' combining the prefix and the original ID to ensure uniqueness. Finally, it merges the layers using the native merge tool and removes the extra 'layer' and 'path' columns. The output is a single merged vector layer with unique stand identifiers.

Prepare VHM and MG input rasters. The script prepares Vegetation Height Model (VHM) and Mixing Degree (MG) rasters for forest stand mapping. It accepts a detailed VHM raster, an MG raster, and a polygon mask. It can optionally convert VHM to byte, reclassify values, clip to mask, and rescale MG values. The VHM is resampled to 10m and 1.5m resolutions. If specified, it generates a binary MG layer reclassified based on deciduous/coniferous thresholds. Outputs include VHM detail, VHM_10m, VHM_150cm, MG_10m, and optionally MG_10m_binary.

Prepare VHM and mixture degree rasters. The script processes high-resolution Vegetation Height Model (VHM) and optionally Forest Mixture Degree (coniferous proportion) raster data into standardized inputs for forest stand mapping. It includes steps like converting VHM to byte data type, clipping to a polygon mask, reclassifying outlier values to NoData, aggregating to 150cm and 10m resolutions with pixel alignment options, rescaling mixture degree values, and creating a binary coniferous/non-coniferous layer. Outputs are raster files used as input for subsequent forest stand map generation.

Optimize spatial join for forest stand mapping. The script performs an optimized spatial join between two vector layers: a primary 'layer to join attribute on' and a secondary 'attribute layer' (expected to be polygonal, e.g., vegetation zones). It ensures performance by first checking and creating a spatial index on the primary layer if missing; converting the secondary layer to singlepart geometries; fixing geometries using the 'Structure' method; indexing the resulting singlepart layer; and finally executing a one-to-one spatial join ('largest overlap only') with intersection predicate. Outputs a vector layer identical in geometry to the primary layer but enriched with selected attributes from the secondary layer, prefixed as specified (e.g., 'VegZone_'). The workflow is explicitly designed for the TBk (Toolkit Bestandeskarte) QGIS plugin used in forest stand map generation.

Calculate DFM confidence map. This QGIS algorithm calculates a DFM (Digital Feature Model) confidence map based on the CRAN decision tree, incorporating ground point density, low vegetation density, and slope. It resamples input rasters to a user-specified cell size, classifies ground point and vegetation densities into confidence categories, reclassifies slope, and combines them using weighted raster calculations to produce a confidence raster. The output is a confidence map that can be used for quality assessment of the DFM and to determine optimal resolution.

Generate archaeological terrain visualizations. The script is a QGIS processing algorithm that generates archaeological terrain visualizations from a user-provided DFM/DEM. It optionally computes Sky-View Factor (SVF), Visualization for Archaeological Topography (VAT via RVT Blender), Openness, Difference from Mean Elevation (DME using WhiteboxTools), and Hillshade. Each output is loaded as a project layer with a name prefix. The algorithm orchestrates multiple child processing steps and provides user-configurable options.

Burn drainage lines into DEM. The script burns vector-based drainage networks into a digital elevation model (DEM) by rasterizing the drainage layers, converting both DEM and drainage to PCRaster format, preparing a boolean drainage mask using cover, and applying a custom 'burndem' algorithm that creates a smooth drop over a user-defined buffer distance and an additional sharp drop directly at the drainage line. The output is a modified DEM raster where elevation values are lowered along and near drainage features to enforce hydrological connectivity.

Delineate stream catchment. The script delineates a stream network and its corresponding catchment boundary from a user-specified outlet point and study extent. It downloads a DEM from OpenTopography (e.g., SRTM or Copernicus), reprojects it, converts it to PCRaster format, computes flow direction using lddcreate, derives Strahler-order streams, snaps the outlet to the nearest stream within a tolerance, calculates the catchment raster via catchment(), and outputs vectorized streams (as line features) and a polygonized catchment boundary (as a single-polygon feature). Intermediate rasters (DEM, flow direction, river, outlet buffer, snapped outlet, catchment) are written to a user-specified folder in PCRaster .map format.

Snap and fix utility network geometries. The script corrects vector geometries by snapping infrastructure layers (aerial boxes, D-cables, F-cables, drop cables, D-ducts) to reference layers (poles, termination boxes, risers, DPs, COs, HPs) and fixes geometries where necessary. It uses QGIS native snapping (with tolerances) and geometry fixing algorithms in a multi-step process to improve topological connections in a utility network.

Snap telecom infrastructure geometries. The script corrects and snaps geometries of telecom network layers (aerial boxes, ducts, drop cables, D‑cables, F‑cables) to corresponding point features (poles, termination boxes, risers, distribution points, central office, household points). It uses QGIS native fix geometries and snap geometries algorithms with a 0.005 tolerance. The workflow first snaps aerial boxes to poles, then snaps ducts to the corrected aerial boxes, and sequentially snaps each cable type to a chain of points after fixing invalid geometries. The outputs are five snapped vector layers: snapped aerial boxes, snapped D‑ducts, snapped D‑cables, snapped F‑cables, and snapped drop cables.

Snap utility network geometries. The script snaps endpoints of cable and duct line features (D-Cables, D-Ducts, F-Cables, DropCables) to reference point layers (Aerial Boxes, Paal, Termination Box, Riser, DP, HPs) within a tolerance of 0.005 degrees. It first fixes geometry errors for cables, then uses QGIS snapgeometries with move-end-points-only behavior. Outputs include five snapped feature layers for aerial boxes, d-ducts, d-cables, f-cables, and drop cables.

Compute confined valley index. The script calculates the Confined Valley Index (CVI) along a river by generating perpendicular transects at a fixed step, intersecting them with left/right river banks and valley bottom polygon to measure distances. It computes the ratio (valley bottom width)/(river bank width) from minimum distances, producing a point layer with attributes: SEZ-ID, VB_RB-index, RB-W, VB-W, minimum distances to each bank, and transect distance.

Calculate river bank distances. The script calculates distances from a river centerline to its left and right banks along the river course. It first generates points at a user-specified step distance along the centerline, creates a simplified centerline from those points, generates perpendicular transects of a given width, and assigns a sequential SEZ-ID to each transect. It then intersects the transects with the left and right riverbank line layers, calculates the coordinates of intersection points, computes the minimum and maximum distances from the centerline to each bank for each transect, and finally joins these attributes back to the transect layer. The outputs include point layers of left and right bank intersections and a transect layer containing fields for the minimum and maximum distances to both banks, enabling river morphology analysis.

Compare riverbank distances between two epochs. The script performs a two-epoch comparison of distances between a river centerline and left/right riverbanks. It creates evenly spaced nodes along the centerline, generates perpendicular transects, intersects them with riverbank lines from two different times, computes per-transect min/max distances for each side and epoch, and outputs a transect layer with delta attributes showing bank migration.

Generate riverbank safety bands. The script generates safety bands (offset lines) from riverbank vectors using erosion rates. It applies single-sided buffers on left and right banks using a multiplicative factor of the erosion rate field, unions the buffers, dissolves them, deletes holes, and converts the resulting polygons to lines. The output is a multiline vector layer representing safety bands at a calculated distance from the riverbanks.

Segment riverbanks and join centerline attributes. The script segments left and right riverbanks using river reach transect limits, calculates the maximum length of transects, and then performs a spatial join by nearest neighbor to transfer attributes from the river centerline reaches to the resulting riverbank segments. The outputs are two vector layers: LRB (left riverbank segments) and RRB (right riverbank segments).

Analyze shop catchment demand. The script computes isochrones (travel-time polygons) around candidate retail shops using the ORS Tools plugin, joins census-based demand points (population per LSOA) to those isochrones, aggregates total population demand per shop-time combination (e.g., 'shopID_5' for 5-minute access), and exports a CSV summarizing total demand per shop and travel time threshold. Inputs are local shapefiles: '_demand_points_census.shp' (census LSOA centroids with 'pop2011_al') and 'candidate_shops.shp' (with 'shopID'); output is 'shops_isochrones_demand.csv' containing columns '_shopID', '_AA_MINS', and 'total'.

Calculate country areas. The script computes the area in square kilometers for each country polygon from the Natural Earth 10m admin 0 countries dataset. It retains only the 'ADMIN' and 'ISO_A3' attributes, reprojects to the World Cylindrical Equal Area projection (ESRI:54034), fixes geometries, calculates the area using $geometry area divided by 1,000,000, and exports the result as a CSV file.

Calculate country area. The script calculates country land areas in square kilometers from the Natural Earth 10m administrative boundaries shapefile. It drops attribute fields, reprojects to world equal-area projection (ESRI:54034), fixes geometries, computes area field 'km2area' using $area/1e6, and reprojects back to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326). The output is a vector layer with the area attribute.

Clean language boundary geometries. The script cleans and standardizes a vector layer of language boundaries (langa.shp) by fixing invalid geometries, adding a unique autoincremental GID field, copying the 'NAME_PROP' attribute into a shorter 'lnm' field, and dropping all other attributes except 'GID', 'ID', and 'lnm'. The final output is a simplified shapefile 'wlds_cleaned.shp' containing only those three fields and topologically valid geometries.

Create vector grid cells with country intersections. The script creates a global 2.5°×2.5° regular grid in WGS84 (EPSG:4326), intersects it with Natural Earth's ne_10m_admin_0_countries polygon layer, dissolves resulting fragments by grid cell ID, cleans geometries using GRASS v.clean (tool=10: 'break' at intersections), fixes geometries again, re-dissolves by cell ID, and exports a final shapefile (vcountries.shp) containing only non-overlapping, topologically clean polygons each assigned a unique integer 'cid' field — representing country-portioned grid cells suitable for spatial aggregation or zonal analysis.

Classify Virtual Countries by Language Intersection. The script classifies virtual country polygons by their intersection with language polygons. It first removes overlapping language polygons using grass7:v.overlay to identify regions without languages, then processes the complementary intersected regions. Both resulting sets are cleaned by fixing geometries, dissolving by cell ID, adding a consistent 'cid' field, and dropping extraneous attributes. The final outputs are shapefiles for virtual countries without languages (TEMP_vcnolangs.shp) and virtual countries with languages (TEMP_vcwithlangs.shp).

Calculate virtual country and water areas. The script calculates the area in square kilometers for virtual country features and the area of water bodies intersecting each virtual country. It first fixes geometries, reprojects to World Cylindrical Equal Area (ESRI:54034), and computes the area of each virtual country feature using the QGIS field calculator, outputting a CSV file (vcareas.csv). It then processes lake data: cleaning with GRASS v.clean, intersecting with virtual countries using v.overlay, dissolving by cell-id, reprojecting, and calculating water intersection area, outputting another CSV (vcwaterareas.csv) after dropping unnecessary fields.

Compute nearest coastal point for centroids. The script computes the closest point on the coastline for each polygon in a shapefile of virtual countries with language attributes. It fixes geometries, computes polygon centroids, uses GRASS v.distance to generate connection lines from centroids to the nearest coast segment, extracts the coastal endpoints of those lines, and outputs a CSV file containing the centroid coordinates (latitude and longitude) and the corresponding coastal point coordinates.

Population and land quality zonal statistics. The script computes zonal statistics (mean) for land quality and population density rasters (years 1500, 1990, 2000) over two vector layers representing virtual countries and areas without languages. It first fixes geometries, then iteratively adds mean raster values to each layer's attributes using QGIS zonal statistics tool, and finally exports the enriched attribute tables as CSV files.

Generate dyad cells from country boundaries. The script creates a 0.5-degree global grid of dyad cells by intersecting a global grid with Natural Earth country boundaries, then cleaning geometries, dissolving by cell ID, dropping extra fields, and outputting a shapefile of land grid cells each with a unique cell identifier for dyadic analysis.

Assign languages to dyad cells. The script assigns language groups to spatially defined dyad cells by joining language polygon geometries (wlds) to dyad cells using fix geometries and join attributes by location. It first fixes geometries of both dyad cells and language regions, then performs a spatial join to attach language identifiers (GID) to each cell, retaining only the cell ID (cid) and language group ID. The result is exported as a CSV file containing which languages are spoken in each dyad cell.

Calculate dyad cell areas and water areas. The script calculates the total area (km²) and water area within dyad cells by processing vector data. It fixes geometries, reprojects to World Cylindrical Equal Area (ESRI:54034), computes area fields using field calculator, intersects with a lakes shapefile using v.overlay, dissolves by cell id, and outputs CSV files with cell id, total area, and water area.

Compute dyad centroid distance to coastline. The script processes a set of dyad cell polygons and a coastline line shapefile to compute for each dyad cell the distance from its centroid to the nearest coastline. It fixes geometries, computes centroids, calculates shortest linear distance using GRASS v.distance, extracts the endpoint on the coast, and outputs a CSV containing each dyad's ID, centroid latitude/longitude, and the latitude/longitude of the closest coastal point.

Create hydrological network. The script generates a hydrological network from a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) using GRASS r.watershed with a user-specified watershed size threshold. It first calculates stream channels as a temporary raster, then converts the raster to a vector layer using r.to.vect, outputting a vector hydro network layer.

Hydro network dispersion from point. The script calculates the watershed dispersion area and hydro network affected by a species occurrence point using a Digital Elevation Model (DEM). It first runs r.watershed with the given threshold to generate flow accumulation, drainage direction, stream network, and basins. Then r.water.outlet uses the drainage raster and point coordinates to delineate the contributing watershed. Rasters are converted to vector layers for streams, sub-basins, and total watershed. Geometry fixes are applied, followed by clipping sub-basins and streams to the total watershed extent. Outputs include vector layers of affected hydro network, affected watershed sub-basins, and the total watershed polygon.

Calculate watershed dispersion. The script calculates the upstream watershed (dispersion) for a given species occurrence point along a river. It uses a DEM to derive drainage direction via GRASS r.watershed, then delineates the contributing area using r.water.outlet, outputting a raster of the watershed dispersion.

Create Species Distribution Overlay Grid. The script creates a grid overlay from a species distribution input. It first generates a grid with user-defined horizontal and vertical spacing over the extent of the input layer. Then it performs an intersect by location to retain only grid cells that overlap the species occurrences. The output is a vector grid of overlapping cells.

Create alien species monitoring points. Creates monitoring points for alien species by intersecting hydro network lines with the boundaries of watersheds or administrative management areas. First, watershed polygon boundaries are extracted as lines. Then, line intersections with the hydro network are computed. Finally, X and Y coordinates are added to the resulting point features.

Calculate potential species range. The script calculates potential species distribution range using a dispersal buffer. It takes a species distribution vector layer and a dispersal distance, buffers the species distribution by that distance with dissolve, then extracts from a reference grid the cells that intersect the buffer, producing a range layer.

Calculate potential species distribution range. The script calculates the potential distribution range of a species by buffering species occurrence data by a dispersal distance, selecting reference grid cells that intersect this buffer, then removing cells that intersect buffered ineffective areas (e.g., barriers, unsuitable habitats). Output is a polygon layer representing the effective range.

Simplify NUTS3 boundaries retaining name and pop. The script simplifies the geometries of the NUTS3 administrative boundaries layer (NUTS3_FIN_pop) using a tolerance of 5000 meters, then retains only the 'name' and 'pop' fields. The result is a simplified layer with reduced geometry and attributes, loaded into the map.

Compute territorial change lines and pins from state maps. The script processes two vector layers representing new and old state maps (SM) for Ukraine, excluding features associated with Ukrainian Armed Forces, to compute territorial changes. It extracts the Autonomous Republic of Crimea boundary, dissolves and buffers geometry, then derives new and old boundary lines via difference operations. It also generates point features along these lines, clips them to relevant areas, and labels them as 'Ukr gains' or 'Ru gains' based on location. Outputs include new lines, old lines, a merged SM output, and a pins layer indicating territorial gains.

Generate Hillshade and Contours. The script takes a DEM raster layer, computes a hillshade with azimuth 300, vertical angle 40, and Z factor 1, then extracts contour lines at 10-unit intervals from the hillshade. Intermediate directories are created. Outputs: a hillshade raster and a contour vector layer.

Create perpendicular lines along line. The script generates perpendicular lines along an input line or polygon layer. It reprojects the input to a specified UTM CRS, then creates points along the line at distances defined by a user-supplied expression (with start and end offsets). Using the native 'points along lines' tool, which adds an 'angle' field, a geometry expression builds perpendicular line segments (e.g., extend(make_line($geometry, project($geometry, 20, radians("angle"-90))), 20, 0)). The resulting lines are optionally reprojected to a target CRS and output as a new line layer.

IDW interpolation of point attribute. The script performs Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) interpolation on an input vector point layer using a user-specified numeric attribute field. It creates a continuous raster surface with defined pixel size and extent, and optionally clips the result to a polygon mask layer using GDAL's clip raster by mask tool. Outputs include the interpolated raster (and clipped version if enabled).
Join multiple layers by location. The script sequentially joins attributes from multiple input vector layers to a base layer using spatial predicates and saves the resulting layer.

Mapped multiple offsets. This QGIS processing script generates a series of parallel offset lines from input line features. It uses a mapping expression (array of (spacing, n) tuples) to iteratively create n offset lines at each specified spacing. Optionally, it can keep the original input lines and apply half spacing to the first and last offsets. The algorithm uses the native:offsetline tool repeatedly, feeding each output as input for the next offset. The final result merges all generated offset lines into a single vector layer.

Calculate TRI, slope, and aspect. The script calculates terrain attributes from a raw digital elevation model (DEM). It first fills sinks using the Wang & Liu method to produce a hydrologically corrected DEM. From this filled DEM, it computes the Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI), slope, and aspect. The outputs are three raster layers: a TRI raster, a slope raster, and an aspect raster, all saved to specified file paths.

Compute Polygonal Smoothness and Continuity. The script computes spatial smoothness and continuity indices for a polygon layer based on a numeric attribute. It first deletes all existing attributes except an auto-increment ID field, then builds a spatial index to identify touching neighbors. For each polygon, it calculates influence as sum of absolute differences in attribute values with its neighbors, treating null/zero neighbors specially. Smoothness is computed as 100 * sum of absolute influences / (number of neighbor connections * attribute value range). Continuity is the percentage of polygons with non-zero/non-null values. The outputs are the processed layer with auto_id and the calculated smoothness and continuity values.

Generate smooth continuous field grid. The script generates a synthetic hexagonal grid of continuous attribute values over a user-defined study area. It begins by creating a grid from the input polygon layer, adds a 'valor' field with initial pseudo-random values, then iteratively adjusts these values using a neighborhood-based smoothness algorithm to achieve a user-specified smoothness (mean absolute difference between adjacent cells normalized by value range) and continuity (percentage of zero-valued cells). The final output includes the grid polygon layer with adjusted 'valor' values and a point layer with random points generated inside each polygon proportionally to the 'valor' values.

Delimit raster variable by influence zone. The script processes a raster layer ('Variable ráster para Maxent') by generating a buffer zone with a user-defined negative distance (interpreted as an inward buffer or erosion), then clips the input raster to that buffered polygon mask. It first creates a zero-valued raster of the same extent, converts it to polygons, applies a buffer with 'Distancia negativa de influencia' (a negative distance value implying contraction), and finally masks the original raster using the buffered polygon. The output is a spatially constrained version of the input raster where peripheral pixels (e.g., near coastlines, borders, islands) are excluded based on the specified inward buffer distance.

Calculate catchment area and hydrologic attributes. The script computes a hydrologically conditioned catchment (watershed) from a user-specified outlet point on a DEM using GRASS GIS r.watershed and r.water.outlet. It generates flow accumulation, flow direction, slope, aspect, stream raster, and stream polygons. For the catchment raster, it optionally produces a vector polygon with derived attributes: area (km²), time of concentration (Tc in hours via Pilgrim’s formula), mean elevation (from zonal statistics on DEM), and optionally mean/min/max slope and aspect (from zonal statistics on slope/aspect rasters), plus outlet elevation extracted directly at the transformed coordinates. All outputs are saved to user-specified destinations.

Classify basins by categorical surface. The script rasterizes a vector layer (e.g., biome or land cover categories) using a specified field (default 'BIOME_INT') into a categorical raster at user-defined resolution, then computes zonal statistics (count, minority, majority) and zonal histograms for each input basin polygon layer. Outputs include one GeoPackage per basin layer containing added histogram columns (e.g., 'HISTO_1', 'HISTO_2') and statistics fields (e.g., '_count', '_minority', '_majority'), all saved to a user-specified folder. The script optionally accepts an existing categorical raster instead of rasterizing.

Compute areal precipitation average. The script computes the areal average precipitation over a catchment by spatially intersecting a gridded precipitation dataset with the catchment boundary, calculating cell areas, assigning weights as the ratio of each cell's area to the total catchment area, and then computing weighted precipitation values (e.g., DATA_20200101_pesata) for each precipitation time step field. Outputs include: (1) clipped grid intersecting the catchment, (2) reprojected precipitation grid (EPSG:32632), (3) clipped grid with added fields 'area_cella', 'area_bacino_const', and 'peso', and (4) final vector layer with weighted precipitation fields appended.

Calculate Waste Dump Volume. The script computes the volume of waste dumps relative to the minimum elevation within the dump area. It clips an input DEM using a waste dump polygon, identifies the minimum positive pixel value, creates a constant raster of that minimum, subtracts it from the clipped DEM to produce a derived DEM of heights above base, and then (incorrectly) calls a constant raster algorithm intended for surface volume calculation to estimate volume.

Calculate scenario-based land area by administrative unit. The script processes multiple input vector layers (e.g., land use or hazard scenario maps), clips each to a mask layer, intersects with functional administrative units (e.g., municipalities), computes area in km² per intersected polygon, aggregates total area per unit (grouped by ISTAT code), and joins results back to the administrative layer — producing a single output vector layer where each administrative unit carries summed area values for each input scenario (e.g., 'alta', 'media', 'bassa' derived from the 'per' field), alongside attributes like ISTAT, Comune, and Provincia.

Aggregate clipped land cover area by administrative unit. The script processes multiple input vector layers (e.g., land cover or risk maps), clips each to a mask layer, intersects the clipped layers with functional administrative units (e.g., municipalities), calculates area in km² for each intersected geometry, and aggregates total area per administrative unit (grouped by ISTAT code), joining results iteratively into a single output layer with one column per input map labeled by its 'per' field value (e.g., 'alta', 'media', 'bassa'). The final output is a vector layer where each administrative unit feature contains fields for ISTAT, Comune, Provincia, and summed area columns named after scenario values extracted from the 'per' attribute of the first feature in each input map.

Map Cities and Boundaries within Area of Interest. The script generates a map layout (PDF) showing cities within an area of interest, clipped regional boundaries, and catchment areas. It first extracts cities intersecting the AOI, then exports a predefined print layout 'Map' to PDF. It applies pre-defined QML styles to regional boundary, catchment area, and the extracted cities, and clips the regional boundary and catchment area to the AOI. The outputs include clipped feature layers and the final map PDF.

Extract OSM roads and railways with half-width. The script extracts road and railway features from an OpenStreetMap line layer, filters by user-selected highway and railway types, clips them to a watershed polygon, and appends a 'demi_emp' (half-width) field based on predefined values (e.g., motorway: 22.5 m, rail: 5.486 m). The resulting layer contains only the OSM lines intersecting the watershed with a half-width attribute, useful for morphological quality index calculations.

Extract and snap stream outlets. The script extracts outlet points from a segmented stream network by interpolating points near the downstream ends of each line segment (using a dynamic distance based on segment length), rasterizes the stream network using a LiDAR-derived 10 m DEM, snaps the interpolated points to the nearest stream pixel within 40 m using WhiteboxTools' JensonSnapPourPoints, and joins the original segment ID attribute (e.g., 'Id_UEA') from the stream network to the snapped points via nearest-neighbor join (max distance 50 m). The output is a point vector layer where each feature represents a snapped outlet with its associated segment identifier.

Extract and merge Quebec transportation networks. The script extracts and merges road, cycleway, and railway networks from Quebec's AQréseau+ dataset within a given watershed area. It first checks the CRS and attribute validity, optionally reprojects layers to the project CRS, clips each network layer to the watershed polygon (if provided), filters out non-relevant features such as tunnels, ferry routes, and certain road classes, merges the three filtered layers into one, and adds a half-width attribute ('demi_emp') based on road classification using predefined values. The output is a unified line vector layer with the transportation network and width attribute.

Calculate A3 morphological quality index. The script calculates the A3 index—a component of the Morphological Quality Index (MQI) for river systems—by quantifying anthropogenic alteration of hydrological and sedimentary regimes and alluvial plain forms at the river segment (UEA) level. It first identifies dams upstream of each river segment within a 1000 m downstream cumulative distance along the network, counting how many dams influence each downstream segment. Then, it computes a 2× mean channel width buffer per segment (using CRHQ PtRef width points), reclassifies MELCCFP land use raster into forest/agricultural/anthropogenic/water classes, calculates proportional agricultural + anthropogenic area within each buffer, and applies a penalty based on upstream dam count. The final A3 score (integer 0–4) is assigned per UEA segment and joined back to the input stream network layer, alongside the raw upstream dam count ('Nb_barrage_amont').

Assess lateral connectivity of rivers. The script calculates the F2 indicator of the Morphological Quality Index (MQI) to evaluate lateral connectivity of river segments with the alluvial plain. It uses input river network (CRHQ), PtRef width points, roads (OSM), and land use raster (MELCCFP). The workflow builds spatial indexes for PtRef, polygons and reclassifies land use (with optional agricultural classes), merges road buffers and land use polygons into a unified obstacle layer, creates perpendicular transects offset from the channel center at each river segment, computes the median first-hit distance to obstacles using a binary search on a prepared geometry engine, and assigns an IQM score (0, 2, 3, or 5) based on predefined distance thresholds. Output is a vector line layer with added fields for median lateral connectivity width and F2 score.

Compute F5 riparian buffer continuity index. The script calculates the F5 morphological quality index for river segments by evaluating the width and longitudinal continuity of functional riparian buffer. It samples transects along river segments, intersects them with a dissolved/simplified riparian forest polygon to measure buffer widths on each side, and computes the proportion of transect length with buffer width >30 m and 15–30 m. These percentages are then classified into an index value (0–4) using predefined thresholds. Outputs include a river network line layer with attributes Perc_15to30m, Perc_gt30m, and Indice F5.

Derive Landsat 7 LST and NDVI. The script computes Land Surface Temperature (LST) and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from Landsat 7 bands: B3 (red), B4 (NIR), and B6 (thermal infrared). It first converts B6 digital numbers to at-sensor radiance using the gain/offset parameters (gain = (12.650 − 3.200)/(255 − 1), offset = 3.200), then applies a single-channel LST inversion: LST = (1282.71 / ln(666.09 / L) + 1) − 273.15 (Kelvin to Celsius), where L is the radiance. NDVI is calculated as (B4 − B3) / (B4 + B3). Both outputs are clipped to a user-provided ROI polygon and styled with QGIS layer styles (NDVI_style_new.qml, LST_style_new.qml).

Extract wind turbine locations from OSM. The script extracts OpenStreetMap (OSM) point features tagged with 'generator:method'='wind_turbine' within a user-defined polygon area of interest. It downloads OSM data via Overpass API, filters for points, clips to the study area, parses the 'height' value from the 'other_tags' field using string operations, and refactors attributes into a standardized output layer with fields: 'nome', 'alturaTorreAer', 'osm_id', 'nome_no_osm', 'geometria_osm', 'nome_osm', and 'alturaTorreAer_osm'. The final output is a vector point layer ('aerogerador_p') containing wind turbine locations and parsed tower height.

Extract OSM park polygons. The script extracts OpenStreetMap (OSM) features tagged with a user-specified key-value pair (default: 'leisure'='park') within a user-defined polygon area of interest. It downloads OSM data via Overpass API, filters for multipolygon geometries, fixes invalid geometries, clips to the input area, converts multipart geometries to single parts, then filters features whose 'name' field matches case-variant substrings of 'Praca', 'pracinha', 'Largo', or 'Parquinho'. Finally, it refactors attributes into standardized fields including 'nome', 'geometriaAproximada', 'turistica', 'osm_id', 'nome_no_osm', 'geometria_osm', and 'nome_osm'. Outputs are two vector layers: one with fixed geometries ('geom') and one filtered and restructured as 'praca_A'.

Identify road displacement features. The script identifies road segments from OpenStreetMap (OSM) that exhibit geometric displacement relative to a reference line layer within a user-defined area of interest. It does so by: (1) querying OSM via Overpass API using configurable OSM key/value tags (default 'highway'); (2) filtering OSM lines to exclude minor paths (e.g., 'path', 'footway', 'track', etc.); (3) clipping both the reference layer and filtered OSM lines to the area of interest; (4) generating 0.000225-degree buffers around both layers; (5) computing the area difference between the OSM buffer and reference buffer; (6) calculating the percentage of excess area (Area_DIF / Area_TOT * 100); (7) selecting OSM features where this percentage exceeds a user-defined threshold (default 40%); (8) joining back original OSM attributes (including 'osm_id', 'name', 'other_tags'); (9) parsing 'ref' values from 'other_tags' to extract route siglas; and (10) outputting a cleaned vector layer with standardized fields: 'osm_id', 'nome', 'geometria_osm', 'nome_osm', 'sigla', 'codtrechorod_osm'. The final output is a feature sink named 'Add_deslocamento_l' containing only displaced road segments meeting the excess-area criterion.

Identify power line segments. The script identifies candidate power line segments by comparing OpenStreetMap (OSM) 'power=line' features against a reference line layer within a user-defined area of interest. It downloads OSM data via Overpass API, buffers both the reference and OSM line layers identically (0.000452 decimal degrees), computes the area difference between buffered OSM and buffered reference geometries, calculates the percentage of OSM buffer area not overlapping the reference buffer ('percentualExtraBaseRef'), filters OSM segments where this excess percentage meets or exceeds a user-defined threshold (default 70%), joins the filtered OSM attributes back to the original clipped OSM lines, extracts description tags from the 'other_tags' field, and outputs a cleaned line layer with fields: 'osm_id', 'nome' (parsed description), 'geometria_osm' (fixed value 'Sim'), and 'nome_osm' ('Sim' if description exists, else 'Não').

Identify road police stations. The script identifies road police stations by querying OpenStreetMap (OSM) for points tagged with key='police' and value='traffic_police', then spatially compares them against a user-provided reference point layer within a defined polygon area of interest. It buffers the reference points (0.000452 decimal degrees), clips OSM-derived points to the area of interest, extracts OSM points that are disjoint from the buffer (i.e., outside the buffer zone), parses the 'name' field from OSM's 'other_tags', and merges the resulting OSM-matched points with the original reference layer—assigning 'Sim' or 'Não' to 'nome_osm' and 'geometria_osm' fields based on presence of OSM name. The final output is a merged vector layer with standardized schema including fields like 'nome', 'osm_id', 'nome_osm', and 'geometria_osm'.

Convert kikker sewer network to GeoDyn format. The script converts municipal sewer infrastructure data from the 'Kikker' system into a GeoDyn-compatible format. It processes three input layers: (1) 'bemalingsgebieden' (catchment polygons), (2) 'kikkerlijnen' (sewer lines), and (3) 'kikkerpunten' (sewer nodes/points). Workflow steps include: fixing geometries of catchments; spatially joining points to catchments via intersection to assign BEM_ID; generating a unique 'BEM_ID' string field (e.g., 'BEM001') for catchments; retaining and propagating BEM_ID as 'BEM_ID_SP' to joined points; joining line attributes (e.g., BERGING_M3, NUMMER) to lines by attribute match on 'NUMMER'; and filtering output fields per layer. Outputs are three feature sinks: (a) 'Gebiedsgegevens_lijn_tbv_stap2_kikker' (lines with NUMMER, VAN_KNOOPN, NAAR_KNOOP, TTOTAAL_M3, BERGING_M3), (b) 'Bemalingsgebieden_tbv_stap2_kikker' (catchments with BEM_ID), and (c) 'Gebiedsgegevens_punt_tbv_stap2_kikker' (points with BEM_ID_SP and other hydraulic attributes). The script is explicitly named 'stap 1.) Kikker to GeoDyn' and belongs to the 'Geodyn cheat' group.

Parse OSM file to layers. The script parses an OSM (OpenStreetMap) file using OGR and QGIS Processing. It reads the file with a provided configuration, extracts point, line, multilinestring, and multipolygon layers, checks and fixes geometry validity, expands the 'other_tags' hstore field into separate attribute columns, adds 'osm_type' and 'full_id' identifiers, optionally applies a subset filter, and outputs the processed layers to GeoPackage, KML, GeoJSON, or Shapefile formats. The result is a set of valid QGIS vector layers ready for further analysis.

Rasterize Building and Tree Heights. The script generates two raster layers for building terrain and tree heights. It rasterizes a building vector layer using a specified height field to produce a 'BuildingTerrain_raster.tif', and then creates variable-distance buffers around tree points based on a radius field, subsequently rasterizing the buffered polygons with the tree height field to output 'Tree_raster.tif'. Both rasters use a common analysis extent and a 0.5m cell size.

Generate Edge-Bundled Flow Map. The script applies edge bundling and optional line merging to create a flow map from input line features. It first preprocesses geometries by fixing, exploding, and removing nulls, then creates Edge objects with optional weight and cluster fields. Edges are grouped into clusters, and force-directed edge bundling is performed on each cluster. If a maximum distance is provided, overlapping segments are collapsed into paths and assigned overlap counts. The result is a flow map line layer with appropriate symbology.

Create TUFLOW Project. The script creates a TUFLOW hydraulic model project within QGIS by setting up project settings (CRS, GIS format, executable), creating a folder structure, generating a domain check vector file, creating empty files, and setting up control file templates. The domain check file is loaded as a styled layer in QGIS.

Assign Elevations to Polygon Vertices. Assigns elevation values to polygon vertices from a DEM raster for TUFLOW TIN processing. The script densifies polygon edges at a user-defined interval (or uses existing vertices), extracts vertices, removes duplicates, samples raster values, and creates a Z field. It outputs a point layer with Z elevation and a polygon layer with Shape_Width set to -1 to indicate TUFLOW should use the generated vertices.

Create classified railway nodes. The script creates a railway node layer from railway segment lines within a specified work area. It extracts start and end vertices from the segments, removes duplicates, counts the number of segments connected at each vertex via spatial join, clips to the work area, and classifies nodes as junction (more than 2 connections), pseudo-node (1 connection), or end-of-line (0 connections). The output is a point layer with a node type attribute.

Classify road nodes by connectivity. The script creates a point layer of road transportation nodes from a line layer of road segments. It extracts start and end vertices, removes duplicates, counts the number of connecting segments per node via spatial join, clips the result to a work area polygon, and classifies each node based on the number of connections: 1 connection marks a road endpoint ('fim de via'), 2 connections marks a pseudo-node, and more than 2 marks a junction. The output layer includes a field 'valor_tipo_no_trans_rodov' with coded types (1 for junction, 3 for pseudo-node, 4 for endpoint).

Export agricultural forest scrubland polygons. The script takes a polygon layer representing agricultural, forest, or scrubland areas, adds a timestamp and a land cover classification code field, and then exports the features into a PostgreSQL/PostGIS table 'area_agricola_florestal_mato' in the public schema via a configured database connection.

Export air transport infrastructure areas. The script exports polygon features representing air transport infrastructure areas to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It first refactors the input layer to add a timestamp field ('inicio_objeto') and a coded value type field ('valor_tipo_area_infra_trans_aereo') from a user-selected enumeration. Then it appends the modified geometry to the 'area_infra_trans_aereo' table in the 'public' schema using the gdal:importvectorintopostgisdatabaseavailableconnections algorithm, with primary key 'identificador'.

Export cable transport infrastructure polygons. The script exports polygon features representing cable transport infrastructure areas into a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table 'area_infra_trans_cabo'. It first adds a timestamp field 'inicio_objeto' using the field refactoring processing tool, then imports the data into the connected database via GDAL's vector import, appending to the existing table with primary key 'identificador' and geometry column 'geometria'.

Export railway infrastructure areas. The script exports polygon features representing railway transportation infrastructure areas to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database (RECART). It first refactors the input polygon layer, adding a timestamp field 'inicio_objeto' and mapping a user-specified field to 'infra_trans_ferrov_id'. Then it uses GDAL's import vector into PostGIS to append the data to the 'area_infra_trans_ferrov' table in the public schema.

Export waterway infrastructure area to PostGIS. The script exports a user-provided polygon layer representing waterway transport infrastructure areas to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It adds a timestamp field ('inicio_objeto') and a selected code for infrastructure type, then imports the processed layer into the 'area_infra_trans_via_navegavel' table using the GDAL import vector into PostGIS tool.

Export work area to PostGIS database. The script imports a polygon layer representing a work area into a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It first refactors the input polygon fields to add metadata including timestamp, date, detail level, name, producer name, and owner name using the Refactor Fields tool. Then it exports the layer to the 'area_trabalho' table in the 'public' schema via GDAL's vector import tool, appending data if the table already exists.

Export artificialized areas to database. Exports artificialized area polygons to a PostgreSQL database. It refactors the input polygon layer by adding a timestamp field 'inicio_objeto' (with value now()) and a field 'valor_areas_artificializadas' with a user-selected value, then imports the layer into the 'areas_artificializadas' table in the 'public' schema using a pre-configured PostgreSQL connection.

Export barrier features to PostgreSQL. The script exports line or polygon features representing barriers to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It first adds two fields: 'inicio_objeto' (current timestamp) and 'valor_barreira' (a barrier type from an enumeration). Then it appends the transformed layer into the 'barreira' table in the public schema of the connected PostgreSQL database using GDAL's import vector tool. The input layer must be a 2D vector layer of lines or polygons.

Export electrical cables to PostgreSQL. The script exports 2D electrical cable line features to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database (RECART). It adds fields for voltage designation and vertical position based on user-selected enumerations, sets a current timestamp, ensures 2D geometry by dropping Z and M values, and then appends to the 'cabo_electrico' table using GDAL's import vector into PostGIS.

Export water conduit to RECART database. The script exports water conduit line features to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database (RECART). It adds attribute fields: a timestamp (inicio_objeto), a water conduit value (valor_conduta_agua) from a code list, and a vertical position value (valor_posicao_vertical) from another code list. The script refactors the fields and then imports the resulting layer into the 'conduta_de_agua' table in the 'public' schema using GDAL's import vector into PostGIS tool.

Export construction polygons to PostGIS. The script exports input point or polygon vector layer to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS table 'constru_polig' by first adding a timestamp field and a construction type field derived from a predefined code list. It uses the GDAL import vector into PostGIS algorithm to append the data to the database using a pre-configured connection. The output is stored in the database, not as a QGIS layer.

Export linear construction to RECART database. The script exports linear construction features (2D lines) to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database (RECART) for infrastructure mapping. It refactors the input layer fields by adding an object start timestamp ('inicio_objeto'), a construction value ('valor_construcao_linear') from a predefined code list, a name ('nome'), a support flag ('suporte'), and a width ('largura'), then removes any Z/M dimensions to ensure 2D compatibility, and finally imports the resulting layer into the 'constru_linear' table in the 'public' schema using GDAL's PostgreSQL available connections provider.

Export contour lines to PostgreSQL. The script exports 3D line layers as contour curves to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It optionally homogenizes Z values by extracting z_majority, refactors fields to add metadata, and sets Z values. If a level of detail is selected, it automatically determines the curve type based on Z spacing.

Export building features to PostgreSQL. The script processes an input point or polygon layer representing building footprints. It refactors the attribute fields, adding a timestamp (inicio_objeto), pre-defined categorical values for building element XY and Z characteristics (valor_elemento_edificio_xy, valor_elemento_edificio_z), and a user-supplied height (altura_edificio). The processed features are then appended to the 'edificio' table in a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database via an existing connection, specifically targeting the RECART database schema.

Export telecom associated elements. The script exports point features classified as 'Elemento associado de telecomunicações' into a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table 'elem_assoc_telecomunicacoes'. It refactors the input point layer by adding an 'inicio_objeto' timestamp field set to now() and a 'valor_elemento_associado_telecomunicacoes' field populated with a selected attribute value from a provided enumeration. The refactored layer is then imported into the public.elem_assoc_telecomunicacoes table using GDAL's vector import into PostGIS function, appending to the existing table and using 'identificador' as primary key.

Export water-associated elements to PostGIS. The script exports water-associated elements (point or polygon) to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It processes an input vector layer by adding a timestamp field and a coded water element type field, removes Z and M dimension values to ensure 2D geometries, and then imports the layer into a 'elem_assoc_agua' table in the 'public' schema of the connected database using GDAL vector import.

Export electricity infrastructure elements. Exports input 2D point or polygon layers representing electricity associated elements to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table named 'elem_assoc_eletricidade'. It first adds a current timestamp field ('inicio_objeto') and a fixed string attribute ('valor_elemento_associado_electricidade') based on a user-selected enumeration. Then it drops Z and M values from the geometry, and finally imports the processed layer into the RECART database using the GDAL 'importvecotorintopostgisdatabaseavailableconnections' algorithm, appending to the target table with a primary key 'identificador' and geometry column 'geometria'.

Export Administrative Boundary Lines to Database. The script exports administrative boundary line features to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It first refactors the input line layer to add fields: 'inicio_objeto' (current timestamp), 'valor_estado_fronteira' (selected boundary state value from a code list), and 'data_publicacao' (publication date). Then it imports the processed layer into the 'public.fronteira' table using the configured PostgreSQL connection.

Export Land-Water Boundary Lines. The script exports 3D line features representing land-water boundaries (shorelines) to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS table 'fronteira_terra_agua' in the RECART database. It first refactors fields to add a timestamp ('inicio_objeto'), a data source date ('data_fonte_dados') from a user-provided date, and an island flag ('ilha'). Then it appends the features to the table without overwriting existing data, using GDAL vector import.

Export aerial transport infrastructure points. The algorithm exports a point layer of aerial transport infrastructure to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table (infra_trans_aereo) using a preconfigured connection. It first refactors the fields, adding an 'inicio_objeto' timestamp and setting 'valor_categoria_infra_trans_aereo' and 'valor_tipo_infra_trans_aereo' from user-selected enumerated values, then imports the layer into the database via GDAL's ImportVectorIntoPostGIS tool.

Export railway infrastructure type points. The script exports a point layer of railway transport infrastructure (Infra Trans Ferrov) to a PostgreSQL database table. It adds two fields: 'inicio_objeto' (current timestamp) and 'valor_tipo_infra_trans_ferrov' (a selected type code) via field refactoring, then appends the features to the 'infra_trans_ferrov' table in the 'public' schema using an existing PostgreSQL connection.

Export road transportation infrastructure points. The script exports road transportation infrastructure point features to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It adds a field 'inicio_objeto' with the current timestamp and a field 'valor_tipo_infra_trans_rodov' with a type code from an enumerated parameter. The refactored layer is then uploaded to the 'public.infra_trans_rodov' table using GDAL's PostgreSQL available connection import.

Export waterway transport infrastructure points to PostgreSQL. This script exports point features of waterway transport infrastructure to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It refactors the input point layer to include a timestamp, a selected type attribute ('valor_tipo_infra_trans_via_navegavel'), and a name. The processed layer is then appended to the 'infra_trans_via_navegavel' table in the public schema, using a pre-configured PostgreSQL connection.

Export classified break lines to PostgreSQL. The script exports 3D line features with classification attributes to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS table 'linha_de_quebra' using a preconfigured connection. It first adds 'inicio_objeto' (current timestamp), 'valor_classifica', and 'valor_natureza_linha' fields via field refactoring, then appends the data to the destination table using GDAL import vector tool. The input must be a 3D line layer. This script is part of the 'Altimetria' group for handling break lines in topographic modeling.

Export margin polygons. The script exports polygon features representing water body margins to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It refactors the input polygon layer by adding an 'inicio_objeto' timestamp field set to current time and a 'valor_tipo_margem' field with a user-selected margin type code from a predefined list. The resulting layer is then imported into the 'margem' table in the 'public' schema of the connected database using GDAL's vector import tool.

Export categorized urban furniture. The script refactors an input point or polygon layer by adding a timestamp field (inicio_objeto) and a type code field (valor_tipo_de_mob_urbano_sinal) based on a user-selected enumeration, then exports the resulting features to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS table named 'mob_urbano_sinal' using GDAL import, appending to existing records.

Export Railway Transport Nodes. The script exports 3D point features representing railway transport nodes (No Trans Ferrov) to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It refactors the input layer to add an 'inicio_objeto' timestamp and a 'valor_tipo_no_trans_ferrov' field based on a user-selected value or an existing field, then imports the refactored layer into the 'no_trans_ferrov' table in the 'public' schema via a pre-configured connection.

Export road transport nodes. The script exports road transport node features from a 3D point layer to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table 'no_trans_rodov'. It first processes the input by adding two fields: a creation timestamp ('inicio_objeto') and the node type attribute ('valor_tipo_no_trans_rodov') taken either from a predefined enumeration value or a user-specified field. The resulting layer is then appended to the existing database table via GDAL import, with geometry column 'geometria' and primary key 'identificador'.

Export Obra de Arte. The script refactors vector polygon input by assigning a timestamp and a type code for 'obra de arte' features, then exports them to the 'obra_arte' table in a PostgreSQL/PostGIS RECART database using a preconfigured connection. The output is stored in the database table.

Export oil, gas, and chemical pipelines. The script exports line vector features representing oil pipelines, gas pipelines, or chemical substances to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table 'oleoduto_gasoduto_subtancias_quimicas'. It first adds an 'inicio_objeto' timestamp using the current time, and encodes selected categorical attributes ('valor_gasoduto_oleoduto_sub_quimicas' and 'valor_posicao_vertical') from enumerator parameters. The refactored temporary layer is then imported into the target database using GDAL's import vector into PostGIS available connections tool.

Export point of interest features. The script exports point or polygon features as points of interest to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table named 'ponto_interesse'. It adds a timestamp field ('inicio_objeto') set to the current time and a string field ('valor_tipo_ponto_interesse') chosen from a predefined code list. The output is a database table with geometry column 'geometria' and primary key 'identificador'.

Export elevation points to PostgreSQL. The script exports 3D elevation point features from a QGIS vector layer to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table named 'ponto_cotado' in the RECART database. It first refactors fields by adding a timestamp ('inicio_objeto') and a classification value ('valor_classifica_las') based on user-selected LAS classification code, then imports the data into the 'public.ponto_cotado' table using GDAL's import vector into PostgreSQL available connections algorithm.

Export waterfall point features. The script exports waterfall point features to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It first refactors the input point layer's fields to add a timestamp field 'inicio_objeto' set to the current date/time, then imports the modified layer into the 'queda_de_agua' table in the 'public' schema using GDAL's 'importvectorintopostgisdatabaseavailableconnections' algorithm. The import appends data to the existing table, uses the 'identificador' primary key, and preserves precision. The script is part of a QGIS processing provider for RECART database operations.

Export Cable Transport Segments. The script exports 2D line features representing 'Segmento da via por cabo' (cable transport segments) to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS RECART database. It first refactors the input layer to add an 'inicio_objeto' timestamp field filled with the current datetime, then imports the layer into the 'public.seg_via_cabo' table using a preconfigured PostgreSQL connection. No spatial or temporal filtering is applied; the entire input dataset is exported.

Export railway segment data. The script processes an input line layer representing railway segments by reformatting fields: adding a timestamp (inicio_objeto), assigning constant attribute values for category, state, vertical position, line type, track type, and electrification status. It then exports the result to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS table 'seg_via_ferrea' using a configured database connection. This algorithm is part of a transport data preparation workflow for the RECART database.

Export road segment to PostgreSQL. The script exports 3D road segment line features to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table 'seg_via_rodov'. It first enriches the input layer with constant attribute fields (estado, physical characteristics, vertical position, direction, road type, number of lanes, paved) using refactoring, then appends the data to the 'public' schema via a configured connection. The output is the populated database table.

Export road limits to database. The script exports road limit line features from a user-defined vector layer to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS table 'via_rodov_limite' in the RECART database. It first refactors fields by adding a timestamp field 'inicio_objeto' set to the current time and a 'valor_tipo_limite' field set to a user-selected value from an enumeration. Then it uses GDAL's vector import tool to append the data to the existing table, preserving primary key 'identificador', with geometry column 'geometria', in schema 'public'.

Export wetland polygons to PostGIS. The script exports a polygon layer of wetland zones (Zona Húmida) to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table 'zona_humida' using a configured connection. It first refactors the input layer's fields by adding a timestamp 'inicio_objeto' set to the current time, a 'valor_zona_humida' attribute selected from an enumeration of wetland value codes, and a boolean 'mare' (tide) flag. The processed layer is then appended to the existing 'zona_humida' table in the public schema, with the geometry column 'geometria' and primary key 'identificador', using the GDAL import vector into PostGIS algorithm.

Characterize seafloor pockmark morphology. The script characterizes pockmarks delineated as polygons using an input DEM. It computes statistical attributes such as depth (mean, min, max, range), volume, slope, and shape metrics (compactness, circularity, convexity, solidity, eccentricity). The workflow involves rasterizing the pockmark polygons, filling depressions in the DEM using SAGA Fill Sinks (Wang & Liu), calculating relative depths, performing zonal statistics on slope and DEM within each polygon, deriving minimum bounding geometry attributes (width, height, angle, aspect ratio), and calculating derived morphological metrics. Optionally, centroids and points of local minima within pockmarks are extracted. Outputs include a characterized polygon layer, centroids, and local minima points.

Calculate flood damage units. The script generates three vector layers of flood damage units (DamUnit3, DamUnit4, DamUnit5) by spatially aggregating flood risk raster values within buffered channel polygons. It first reprojects and resamples a primary flood risk raster (floodriskrastermap) to a user-defined damage unit cell size, converts it to polygons, intersects those with a SWAT+ channel buffer, assigns unique IDs, then computes zonal statistics (sum) for multiple flood risk rasters (A–E) over each damage unit polygon. Finally, it multiplies each raster’s sum by the pixel area (pixelsizem²) to obtain total damage estimates per unit and aggregates results by damage unit ID (duid), producing three outputs differing in included risk layers: DamUnit3 (A+B+C), DamUnit4 (A+B+C+D), and DamUnit5 (A+B+C+D+E).script_55730.py,Natural hazards,Estimate flood risk mitigation potential,[],,None to None,The script computes flood risk mitigation metrics including probability indices (PIa–PIe) and expected annual damage differences (EADD3–EADD5) for administrative units, using SWAT+ hydrological model outputs (channel flow statistics), damage unit maps, and return period parameters. It calculates MDFT (mean discharge frequency threshold) values using Gumbel distribution formulas, derives probability indices via double exponential (Gumbel) transformation, aggregates results by channel or administrative ID, and computes population change-adjusted risk reduction percentages (AvgPobChg3/4/5) and spatially aggregated EADD values per administrative unit. Outputs include vector layers with AvgPobChg3/AvgPobChg4/AvgPobChg5 and EADD3/EADD4/EADD5 fields joined to administrative boundaries.

Passive visibility analysis with parameter variations. The script computes passive visibility rasters for an observed point or polygon, incorporating multiple parameter variations: the number of contour points for polygons, above-ground feature heights (sursol) with differentiated or global variations, observer height, target height, and analysis radius. It processes a DEM (MNT) raster and optional sursol shapefile/CSV to generate digital surface and elevation models. For each combination of parameter values, it runs a viewshed algorithm, producing binary and fuzzy GeoTIFF rasters and an optional web visualization output.

Visibility analysis data preparation. The script prepares data for passive visibility analysis by clipping raster elevation models (MNT, MNE, MNS) to a buffer around an observation point, merging vector surface cover layers (sursol) with attribute assignment based on a CSV configuration, and generating combinations of height variations for multi-parameter analysis.

Multi-parameter passive visibility computation. This QGIS processing algorithm computes multiple passive visibility rasters by varying parameters: observer height, target height, number of contour points for polygon targets, and surface height (using DTM and optional surface shapefiles with CSV). It iterates over all parameter combinations, for each point (or random points on polygon contour) runs the Choucas:visibilitepassive viewshed algorithm, and for polygon targets combines per-point visibility so that a pixel is visible only if all points are visible. Outputs are GeoTIFF rasters saved in a user-specified folder, with optional web visualization.

Convert CSV depth data to grid. The script reads CSV files with longitude, latitude, and depth (Z) columns, creates a point shapefile, optionally calculates an optimal grid resolution based on point density, and generates a raster depth grid using QGIS processing tools.
