Compute GLCM texture measures. The script is a QGIS plugin for computing Grey Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture features from a raster image. It allows the user to select an input raster layer, choose a GLCM measure (contrast, dissimilarity, homogeneity, energy, entropy, ASM, standard deviation, or mean), and set parameters (block size, sampling distance, number of grey levels, pixel pair angle). It then rescales the input to 0-255, digitizes the image into levels, computes GLCM matrices over a moving kernel using OpenCV warping and filtering, and calculates the selected measure per pixel. The output is a GeoTIFF raster file added to the QGIS project, along with a text info file detailing the parameters used.

Bathymetric morphometry analysis. The BathyMorph QGIS plugin processes a digital bathymetric model (DEM) to fill no-data gaps using interpolation, then calculates slope, contours, roughness, generates a higher-resolution interpolated DEM via TIN interpolation, and computes the Bathymetric Position Index (BPI) using inner and outer smoothing radii. Outputs include interpolated raster, slope raster, contour shapefile, roughness raster, high-resolution raster, and BPI raster, with optional standardization. The user selects input raster and output paths via a dialog; outputs are added to the QGIS map canvas.

Classify Seafloor Benthic Terrain. The script classifies benthic terrain from an input bathymetry raster. It computes broad-scale and fine-scale Bathymetric Position Index (BPI) using specified inner/outer radii via OTB mean smoothing and raster calculations, standardizes the BPI rasters, calculates slope, and then applies a classification dictionary (CSV, Excel, or XML) to categorize each cell into geomorphic zones (e.g., Peak, Ridge, Flat, Depression). The classified raster is converted to polygons, filtered with sieving to remove small fragments, aggregated by class, joined with zone names, and saved as a shapefile and a raster output, along with an information text file.

Estimate multibeam sonar coverage. The script estimates the coverage area of a multibeam sonar beam given a trackline shapefile and a bathymetry raster. It first generates points along the trackline at a spacing derived from the bathymetry raster statistics, then samples depth values at those points, calculates a coverage radius as depth * tan(half-swath angle), buffers the points by this radius, dissolves the overlapping buffers, and outputs a coverage polygon shapefile. The final polygon is added to the QGIS map. Additionally, a text file with processing details is created.

Object-Based Segmentation and Zonal Statistics. The script performs object-based image analysis on multi-band raster images. It rescales user-provided input bands (2-5) to a common 0-254 range, builds a virtual raster, applies Orfeo ToolBox KMeans classification to generate an initial segmentation, sieves out small clusters based on a user-defined minimum size, converts the raster to vector polygons, aggregates polygons by cluster value, and computes zonal statistics (mean and standard deviation) for each input band per polygon. The final output is a shapefile with random colors assigned to each class.

Generate raster coverage polygon. The script creates a polygon shapefile representing the spatial coverage of a raster layer. It uses a raster calculator to assign a value of 1 to all valid cells, polygonizes the temporary raster, deletes holes, and outputs a shapefile. The resulting polygon is added to the QGIS map project.

Bathymetry tree artifact removal. The script removes spurious pixel artifacts resembling trees from bathymetry raster data in QGIS. It first applies a median filter of a user-specified radius, computes the difference between the original and filtered rasters, then replaces pixels where the absolute difference exceeds a threshold with the median-filtered value while retaining original values within the threshold. The cleaned bathymetry raster and a slope raster derived from it are saved and added to the map with grayscale contrast enhancement.
Download GeoDanmark vector data. Downloads GeoDanmark data for a selected entity type from Datafordeler API, unzips it, and loads it as a vector layer.

Download Cadastral Data. The script downloads cadastral data from the Danish Datafordeler API. It authenticates with a username and password, selects an entity type (e.g., BygningPaaFremmedGrundFlade) and data type (current, bitemporal, or temporal), constructs a download URL for a GeoPackage file, downloads the file using the QGIS file downloader, unzips it, and extracts all features into a QGIS vector layer.

Create empty vector layer for area drawing. The script creates an empty vector layer (any geometry type) with CRS EPSG:4326 intended for manual digitizing of property or implementation areas in QGIS. The process uses the specified spatial extent to generate a template layer, extracts features with an impossible expression to ensure emptiness, and refactors fields to produce the final output file.

Refactor and dissolve property polygons. The script refactors and dissolves vector layers (polygons, lines, points) to create a single clean polygon shapefile for a given ID_Area. It merges inputs, converts polygons to lines and centroids, explodes lines, polygonizes, joins attributes by location, adds an 'id' field, dissolves by id, and outputs a refactored shapefile with fields 'id' and 'dt_arquivo' ready for submission to the HorusBI validation platform.

Merge OSPAR BH3 disturbance layers. The script prepares a merged seabed physical disturbance dataset for subsequent R analysis by combining two OSPAR BH3 region vector layers (CNS and NCS) from a VMS-derived Geopackage. It fixes geometries, reprojects both layers to EPSG:4326, creates spatial indexes, adds a region label field ('CNS' or 'NCS'), merges the labeled layers, adds an integer unique ID field (ess_unique_id) using row numbers, and finally fixes geometries of the merged result. The output layer 'sl1_bh3_merged_disturbance' is a vector layer in WGS84 with original geometry and label attributes.

Generate OSPAR sub-regions boundaries. The script processes the OSPAR reporting units vector layer to produce dissolved sub-region boundaries for the 2018 and 2025 reporting cycles. It fixes geometries, reprojects to EPSG:4326, creates a spatial index, filters specific Level 2 regions (L2.2.7, L2.3.2, L2.3.3, L2.5.2, L2.1.9, L2.1.3, L2.2.4, L2.2.8, L2.2.9), refactors fields to assign region codes (NNS for Northern North Sea, NCS for North Central Sea) to two time-boundary attributes, and dissolves the features by these code fields to generate a single boundary dataset with attributes for 2018 and 2025 sub-regions.

Calculate dissolved Scottish marine region area. The script fixes geometries, reprojects to EPSG:4326, creates a spatial index, and dissolves the input Scottish marine assessment regions into a single polygon. It then calculates the area in square kilometers (field scottish_region_areakm2) and writes the dissolved result as output.

Clip OSPAR subregions to Scottish waters. The script clips OSPAR sub-regions (2018 and 2025 boundary versions) to Scottish marine regions using intersection, then dissolves by temporal boundary identifiers ('subreg2018', 'subreg2025'), calculates area in km², fixes geometries, promotes to multipart, and performs final dissolution by boundary flag ('2018_bound' or '2025_bound') to compute total dissolved area per year. Outputs include clipped+attributed 2018/2025 subregion layers, dissolved Scottish waters layers for each year, and total area summaries (km²) for both years.

Batch clip seafloor disturbance. The script prepares seafloor disturbance data for spatial analysis by performing a batch clip operation. It first generates a grid based on the extent of the disturbance layer, then clips the disturbance layer by the grid, and subsequently clips the result by a dissolved 2018 area polygon. The outputs are an interim clip and a final clipped vector layer for 2018.

Batch clip seafloor disturbance 2025. The script clips a merged seafloor disturbance vector layer by a grid created from its extent, then further clips the result by a dissolved area calculation layer to produce a final clipped output for 2025.

Merge and dissolve protected area layers. The script processes marine protected area (MPA) and special area of conservation (SAC) vector layers for Scotland. It refactors fields to a common schema, extracts features by attribute (MPA_NETWOR='Y' and UPDATED <= '2020-12-31'), fixes geometries, merges the layers, and then dissolves boundaries to produce a merged and dissolved protected area dataset. Outputs include a merged layer and a dissolved layer.

Slim merged seafloor boundaries 2018. The script processes vector seafloor feature data for 2018 to prepare it for R analysis. It merges attributes from subregion boundaries, retains key fields (ess_unique_id, original_areakm2), deduplicates by feature ID, calculates clipped area in km2, and fills missing subregion codes with 'NNS'. The outputs include cleaned feature layers with subregion, area, and unique identifiers.

Calculate seafloor feature area by subregion. The script prepares seafloor integrity spatial data for further analysis by merging a clipped output layer with a dissolved subregion boundaries layer, retaining selected fields, performing a spatial join to assign subregion identifiers, removing duplicate features based on a unique ID, and calculating the area in square kilometers for output features. It outputs a refined clipped layer with subregion assignment and computed area.

Identify features within MPAs 2018. The script identifies features (e.g., seafloor features) that intersect with marine protected areas (MPAs) in 2018. It takes a pre-clipped feature layer with area and subregion attributes and a dissolved MPA layer, creates spatial indices, refactors fields to retain key attributes (unique ID, original area, subregion, clipped area), and performs a one-to-one spatial join by location (intersect) to tag each feature with MPA membership. The output is a vector layer containing features with MPA and subregion information, ready for further R analysis.

Identify features within MPAs 2025. This script identifies which spatial features from a 2025 seafloor integrity dataset intersect with Marine Protected Areas (MPAs). It creates spatial indices for both input layers, refactors the feature layer fields to keep essential attributes (unique ID, original area, subregion, clipped area), and performs a one-to-one spatial join (intersect) to append MPA attributes to the features. The output is a vector layer with feature attributes and MPA information, used prior to statistical analysis in R.

Compute subbasin curve number. The script processes vector layers of subbasins, land cover, and soil type to compute SCS curve number (CN) and related hydrologic attributes. It reprojects inputs, fixes geometries, performs spatial intersections, and uses field calculator with CASE expressions to assign HSG, land cover retardance class, runoff coefficient class, Manning's n, retardance coefficient, and CN based on land cover class and soil type. Finally, it calculates area in hectares and outputs a polygon layer with curve number and other fields for each intersected polygon.

Calculate SCS lag time for subbasins. The script calculates SCS lag time for each subbasin by intersecting land cover and soil data to derive hydrologic parameters (curve number, Manning's n) and uses WhiteboxTools to compute longest flow path and average slope from a DEM. It outputs a CSV summary of basin area, weighted CN, weighted n, flow path length, slope, and lag time.

Watershed delineation and discharge calculation. This script delineates watersheds and subbasins using WhiteboxTools from a DEM and an outfall point, integrating land cover and soil data to compute hydrological parameters. It calculates time of concentration using multiple methods (Kirpich, Izzard, FAA, SCS, Kinematic Wave) for various return periods from a regression CSV, then estimates peak discharge via the rational method. Outputs include a basin summary CSV file and intermediate rasters/vectors.

Catchment delineation from DEM and outfall. The script delineates a watershed (catchment) and its subbasins given a DEM and an outfall point. It reprojects the DEM to a target CRS, fills sinks, computes flow accumulation and direction to generate streams and basin rasters using a minimum area threshold. It thins the stream raster, converts to vector, then snaps the outfall point to the nearest stream. Using the drainage direction raster, it extracts the watershed upstream of the snapped outlet point. After fixing geometries, it clips the subbasin polygons to the delineated basin and extracts detailed stream vectors. Outputs: stream vector layer, watershed basin polygon, and subbasin polygons.

Generate curve number using land cover and soil. The script computes SCS curve numbers for subbasins by intersecting reprojected land cover and soil type vector layers and assigning curve numbers based on land cover class and hydrologic soil group. It first reprojects the input land cover and soil layers to a common CRS, fixes geometries, then intersects the subbasins with the land cover layer, and further intersects with the soil layer. Using field calculator, it adds attributes for retardance coefficient class and numeric value, runoff coefficient, Manning's n, and the curve number derived from a lookup table evaluating land cover class and HSG group. The output is a vector layer with these attributes and area in hectares.

Plot river transect water surface profiles. This QGIS processing algorithm generates river cross-section profile plots for each transect line by sampling terrain elevation from a user-supplied terrain raster and water surface elevation (WSE) from multiple WSE rasters (e.g., HEC‑RAS output). For each transect feature, it creates points along the line at 1‑meter intervals, extracts terrain and WSE values via raster sampling, and combines them in a matplotlib plot with terrain in black and each WSE scenario in a distinct color. The final plot images are saved as PNG files, enabling visual comparison of water surface profiles under different hydraulic conditions.

Extract RAS flow and thalweg attributes. The script provides a GUI to extract maximum flow characteristics (discharge, velocity, flow area, water surface elevation, energy grade line) from HEC-RAS plan HDF5 files along user-specified reference lines, and computes the lowest terrain elevation (thalweg) by sampling points along each line from a terrain raster. It outputs summary CSV and HTML files containing these attributes for each reference line and flow scenario.

Compute polygon overlap density. The script calculates the density of overlapping polygons in a vector layer. It first runs a union operation (with overlay set to None, presumably as a placeholder), then aggregates features by geometry to count overlapping polygons and optionally concatenate a list of unique source IDs. A filter step retains only polygons with overlap counts greater than or equal to a user-specified threshold. The final output is a polygon vector layer with an 'NUMPOINTS' field and, if a unique ID field is provided, an 'ID_LIST' field listing contributing polygon IDs.

Download Copernicus Land Cover Data. The script downloads Copernicus Global Land Cover data tiles from an S3 bucket for a user-specified product, year, and spatial extent. It uses a predefined S3 object listing to identify available tiles, applies filtering based on selected products and years, optionally generates a grid to extract tile codes intersecting the input extent, and downloads the matching GeoTIFF files to a local directory.

Prepare vector predictors for land cover change modeling. The script prepares vector datasets for MOLUSCE land cover change modeling by generating a raster aligned to a reference raster’s spatial domain (CRS, extent, rows/columns, pixel alignment). It supports two evidence-based modes: (1) Presence mode — rasterizes vector features (points, lines, polygons), optionally buffered and optionally using a numeric field value or constant 1; (2) Proximity mode — first rasterizes features as binary presence, then computes Euclidean distance to nearest feature, with output units selectable as georeferenced (e.g., meters) or pixels. Output is a single-band raster matching the reference raster’s geometry exactly.

Resample Copernicus land cover. The script resamples Copernicus Global Land Cover (CGLS) 333m raster products to 1km resolution while preserving the spatial extent of legacy 1km time series. It first reclassifies input raster values using a user-defined table (e.g., mapping [-0.08,0.92,1,0.92,255,0] to recode invalid pixels), then performs two parallel GDAL translate operations: one with 'average' resampling (for continuous variables like NDVI/FAPAR/LAI) and one with 'mode' resampling (for categorical land cover), followed by a raster calculator multiplying the two outputs, and finally compresses and exports the result as a GeoTIFF. The workflow is explicitly tuned for Copernicus vegetation biophysical variables (NDVI, FAPAR, LAI) and references CGLS PROBA-V and Sentinel-3 origins.

Articulate image coverage areas. The script processes a vector layer named 'edicao_articulacao_imagem_a' to identify, aggregate, and spatially order image acquisition footprints (by sensor name and date) overlapping a given map area feature. It computes pole-of-inaccessibility radii to filter features based on label placement suitability (>400 m relative to map area), clips and reprojects the layer to EPSG:4674 (SIRGAS 2000), aggregates overlapping geometries by sensor and date, inserts synthetic features representing uncovered areas (via symmetrical difference), sorts features chronologically and by sensor, applies rule-based labeling with sequential numbering (1–N), and generates an HTML table listing ordered image acquisitions (with sensor and date) in a multi-column layout for insertion into a QGIS print layout. Outputs include a styled and labeled vector layer, updated layer list, and populated HTML table item ('tabela_articulacao_imagens') in the composition.

Identify label overlap. The script identifies overlapping labels in vector layers within a geographic boundary at a specified map scale. It extracts label positions using QGIS's native label engine, filters to selected layers, computes precise label polygon geometries using a label size calculator, then performs spatial analysis (intersection, dissolve, spatial join) to detect overlapping areas. The output is a polygon layer of flagged overlapping label regions.

Insert energy tower symbols. The script inserts point features representing energy transmission towers along energy transmission lines, clipped to a map frame polygon. It chops the input line layer into segments at regular intervals (scaled by map scale), extracts the start points of each segment, computes rotation angles for symbol orientation, filters out points coincident with line endpoints (boundaries), and populates a target point layer (edicao_simb_torre_energia_p) with those points and attributes (simb_rot, visivel). Finally, it removes any inserted tower points that fall within a user-defined distance (in mm at map scale) from the frame boundary lines.

Insert road segment markers. The script inserts road segment identifier points (markers) along linear road features based on their length, scale-dependent spacing rules, and proximity constraints relative to a frame polygon. It filters roads by non-null 'sigla' attribute, dissolves by 'sigla' and 'tipo', clips to the frame, splits at intersections and frame boundaries, places points at scale-dependent fractional distances (e.g., 15%, 50%, 85% for long segments), removes points within a scale-derived minimum distance of the frame boundary, and writes multiple offset marker points per multi-sigla feature (e.g., 'BR-101;SP-123') into an existing point layer with attributes 'sigla', 'jurisdicao', 'visivel', and 'tipo'. No new layers are returned—modifications are applied in-place to the input MARKER layer.

Adjust contour curve orientation. The script adjusts the geometric orientation (clockwise or counterclockwise) of line features representing contour curves in a QGIS vector layer. It identifies contours whose current vertex order does not match the requested orientation (using a signed area heuristic via cross products over sliding 3-point windows), extracts those features, reverses their direction using QGIS's native:reverselinedirection algorithm, and updates the original layer in-place with the corrected geometries. No new output layer is returned; edits are applied directly to the input layer.

Estimate bathymetric depth. The script implements a multi-phase satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) pipeline that estimates water depth from multispectral optical imagery. It begins by optionally clipping the input raster using a user-provided water mask polygon (with reprojection, geometry fixing, and optional edge shrinking). Training and validation point layers are reprojected and filtered by depth threshold. Phase 1 performs preprocessing: band selection (coastal, blue, green, red, NIR), optional sunglint correction, water masking (via OTSU, manual threshold, or band math), and feature stack generation. Phase 2 applies RANSAC-based outlier filtering on training points using residuals from initial band-ratio models. Phase 3 fits multiple machine learning algorithms (RF, GB, ET, SVR, MLP) to the feature stack and training points to generate an initial depth map. Phase 4 optionally refines this map using adaptive retraining with additional in-situ points. Final outputs undergo clamping to max_depth, optional removal of positive (non-physical) depth values, and optional slope-based spatial filtering. The workflow produces two primary rasters: 'Initial SDB Map [Phase 3]' and 'Refined SDB Map [Phase 4]', both added to QGIS project upon completion.

Clean bathymetric depth map. The script provides raster processing functions to clean a bathymetric depth map by removing positive values (above-water pixels) via rasterio, clamping excessively deep anomalies beyond 1.5 times a maximum depth threshold while masking invalid areas using a feature stack, and filtering out steep slopes exceeding a user-defined threshold. It leverages QGIS processing algorithms (gdal:rastercalculator and gdal:slope) and outputs cleaned depth raster files.

Estimate water depth. The script executes a multi-phase bathymetric inversion pipeline for Satellite-Derived Bathymetry (SDB) using optical satellite imagery. It performs pre-processing (Phase 1: band selection, sun glint correction, water masking, feature stack generation), point-based filtering (Phase 2: RANSAC outlier removal on training points), global modeling (Phase 3: ensemble ML regression—Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Extra Trees, SVR, MLP—to predict depth from spectral features), optional adaptive refinement (Phase 4: localized model retraining using additional adaptive training points), and post-processing (clamping to max_depth, removing positive-depth pixels, slope-based depth filtering). Outputs include Phase 3 initial depth map, Phase 4 refined depth map, clipped feature stacks, water masks, cleaned/filtered rasters, and validation reports if enabled.

Clean and slope-filter depth map. The script performs post-processing on a depth map raster. It removes deep anomalies using a threshold derived from max depth (1.5 × max, or -100 as default), masks out invalid pixels via a feature stack raster, applies a slope filter to retain only areas with slope below a user-specified threshold (in degrees), and eliminates remaining positive values (≥0) using rasterio masking. The processing relies on GDAL raster calculator and slope algorithms through QGIS Processing, producing a cleaned depth raster as final output.

Multi-criteria suitability modeling. This script provides a QGIS processing base class for multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) suitability modeling. It includes common geospatial operations such as clipping vector and raster layers to a study area, fixing geometries, reprojecting, rasterizing vector features, generating proximity maps, classifying raster values by distance thresholds or numeric thresholds, normalizing layers, and merging weighted layers to produce composite suitability rasters.

Compute USPED erosion flux. The script computes the USPED (Unit Stream Power-based Erosion Deposition) model output raster, which estimates spatially distributed net erosion/deposition rates. It does so by: (1) computing flow accumulation (using SAGA's top-down MFD algorithm), slope, and aspect from a filled DEM; (2) deriving sflowtopo — a topographic predictor combining flow accumulation and slope with exponentiated sine (rill mode) or linear (sheet mode); (3) multiplying sflowtopo by K-C-R factor rasters (or scalar defaults) and directional cosines/sines of rotated aspect to compute qsx and qsy sediment transport components; (4) computing slope and aspect of qsx and qsy rasters; (5) calculating directional derivatives qsx_dx and qsy_dy using tan(slope) × cos/sin of rotated aspect; and (6) summing the derivatives (with ×10 scaling for sheet erosion mode) to produce the final USPED raster. The Flow Accumulation raster is also output separately.

Split RGB bands from input image. The script splits an input raster image into its Red, Green, and Blue spectral bands using SAGA's 'splitrgbbands' algorithm, then converts each extracted band (R, G, B) to a standardized format via GDAL Translate—preserving CRS and data type—producing six outputs: three raw band rasters (BLUE, GREEN, RED) and three converted rasters (R_conv, G_conv, B_conv). The workflow is strictly band decomposition and format conversion; no spectral index calculation, classification, or temporal/spatial filtering is performed.

Generate attribute-based description. The script adds a new text field 'description' to an input vector layer by executing a user-defined Python function that maps feature attributes (via a dictionary of field names and values) to a descriptive string; it also adds a second text field 'metadata' containing a JSON-serialized dictionary built from user-provided key-value pairs in a matrix parameter. The output is a new vector layer with these two additional fields.

Compute polygon medial axis skeleton. The script computes a medial axis (skeleton) of an input polygon geometry using a Voronoi-based approach: it generates points along or at vertices of the polygon boundary, constructs Voronoi polygons from those points, converts them to lines, filters line segments lying within the input polygon, dissolves and simplifies the resulting medial axis, optionally applies directional merging to reduce branches, and — if postprocessing is enabled — extracts and extends the longest line segment to intersect with the original polygon boundary. The output is a QgsFeature generator (iterable of QgsFeature objects) representing the final skeleton geometry (or the single longest intersected line after extension and clipping).

Generate Voronoi polygons from points. The script generates Voronoi tessellations from input point features (e.g., random points inside polygons or centroids of k-means clusters) using QGIS processing algorithms. It supports two main workflows: (1) splitting a polygon layer into Voronoi-derived subregions via random point generation, k-means clustering, centroid extraction, buffering, and intersection; and (2) computing Voronoi-based medial axes/skeletons for linear features. Outputs are vector layers — either intersected Voronoi polygons clipped to input boundaries or simplified, dissolved, directional-merged skeleton lines.

Filter and intersect CAR with MapBiomas Alerta. The script filters a CAR (Cadastro Ambiental Rural) shapefile to retain only polygons where the 'des_condic' attribute contains the substring 'analise', then intersects those filtered polygons with a MapBiomas Alerta (MP) shapefile. It dissolves the intersection results by 'cod_imovel', retains only the 'cod_imovel' field, reprojects the result to EPSG:31982 (UTM zone 22S, Brazil), calculates area in hectares, and saves the final layer as a GeoPackage file named 'results_pyqgis.gpkg'. No raster or time-series operations are performed; all steps are vector-based GIS processing using QGIS native algorithms.

Download and clip digital elevation model. The script downloads digital elevation models (DEM) for a user-defined extent in QGIS. It supports SRTM, Copernicus DEM GLO-30, FABDEM, ANADEM, and GMTED2010. It automatically determines the required tiles, downloads them from remote URLs, decompresses SRTM data, merges multiple tiles into a virtual raster, and clips the result to the specified extent. The output is a GeoTIFF raster file, optionally loaded into QGIS with a selected symbology style.

Clean vector geometry. The script performs a light geometric cleanup on an input vector layer by (1) removing features with null or empty geometries directly from the original layer and logging their IDs and attributes to a no-geometry output table, and (2) removing duplicate vertices from line and polygon features using QGIS's native:removeduplicatevertices algorithm. It does not fix or delete invalid geometries. The output includes the modified input layer (in-place edits) and a separate attribute-only table containing the deleted features' original attributes plus auxiliary fields 'lf_orig_id' and 'lf_reason'.

Extract river headwater points and lines. The script identifies and extracts river headwaters (springs) from a vector stream network layer using topological dangle detection and length-based filtering. It first dissolves the input line layer, detects dangles (endpoints with degree 1) as candidate headwaters, splits the dissolved network at duplicate vertices (to isolate individual segments), extracts segments intersecting the dangle points, computes segment lengths ($length), filters segments by user-defined length criteria (Minimum Value: ≤ VALUE; Maximum Value: ≥ VALUE; ALL: no filter), removes segments overlapping a buffer around the provided 'River Mouth' point layer (to exclude mouth artifacts), and outputs two results: (1) Headwater_Lines — filtered line segments retaining only a 'Compri' (length) attribute, and (2) Headwater_Points — point features derived from the intersection of original dangles and filtered headwater lines, preserving original layer attributes plus length.

Count polygon overlaps per point. The script counts and concatenates ISO codes from intersecting polygons for each point feature, then computes statistics (count) grouped by the concatenated ISO values. It loads two vector layers (polygons and points), adds a 'poly_boundary' string field to the points layer populated with comma-separated 'iso' attribute values from all polygons that intersect each point, commits the edits, runs 'Statistics by Categories' to count occurrences per unique 'poly_boundary' group, and finally drops all statistical fields except the count, saving the result to 'output.gpkg'. The script prints field names of the polygon layer and the computed 'poly_boundary' values for verification.

Smooth Voronoi polygons by jittering vertices. The script generates smoothed Voronoi tessellations from input point features, constrained to a base polygon layer (e.g., country or administrative boundary). It first computes standard Voronoi polygons, clips them to the base map, densifies polygon boundaries with additional vertices, randomly perturbs each vertex within a user-defined tolerance, reconstructs closed polygon paths from the jittered vertices, buffers the resulting lines to fill gaps, clips again to the base map, and finally joins original point attributes back to the smoothed polygons. The output is a vector layer of smoothed, topologically valid Voronoi-derived polygons retaining original point identifiers and attributes.

Sample raster pixel values. The script performs spatial sampling of a user-provided raster layer by generating point features at pixel centers and selecting a user-defined number of points either randomly (unstratified) or stratified by reclassifying the raster into quantiles, equal intervals, or K-means classes. For stratified sampling, it first applies a custom classification algorithm ('Precision Agriculture:R - Classification'), converts the classified raster to points, filters out 'nan' values, then performs random selection within each class subset. The final output is a vector layer of sampling points with added X/Y coordinate fields.

Create convex hull envelope. The script computes the convex hull polygon enclosing all input point features. It first dissolves the input point layer (though dissolution has no effect on points without grouping fields), then applies QGIS's native convex hull algorithm to generate a single polygon output representing the minimal convex envelope around the point set. The output is a vector layer (polygon geometry) written to the specified destination.

Orient grid to row direction. The script generates an oriented vector grid aligned with the dominant direction of points in an input point layer, where point order reflects data acquisition sequence (e.g., along crop rows or machine pass). It computes the median heading angle from consecutive point pairs, rotates a buffered extent-based grid around the centroid by the negative of that angle, and outputs the rotated grid as a vector layer. The grid cell size is user-defined in meters, and manual rotation override is supported.

Interpolate soil attribute values. The script performs spatial interpolation of a user-specified numeric field (e.g., soil nutrient concentration, pH, or moisture) from point vector data to generate a continuous raster surface. It supports four methods: Thiessen (nearest-neighbor tessellation), Voronoi (geometric partitioning), Delaunay triangulation (with attribute joining), and Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) via GRASS v.surf.idw. For tessellation methods, it first creates polygons (Thiessen/Voronoi/Delaunay), clips them to the convex hull of input points, then rasterizes the resulting vector layer using the specified field and pixel resolution. For IDW, it directly invokes GRASS IDW interpolation. Outputs are a single GeoTIFF raster at user-defined grid resolution (meters).

Generate tessellation polygons from points. The script generates spatial tessellations (Thiessen/Voronoi polygons or Delaunay triangulations) from an input point vector layer. For Thiessen/Voronoi methods, it computes the tessellation, derives a convex hull from the input points, and clips the tessellation to that hull. For Delaunay, it performs triangulation and joins attributes from the original points via spatial location. The output is a raster destination layer (though the algorithm logic actually produces vector geometries — indicating a mismatch between parameter type and actual processing, as QgsProcessingParameterRasterDestination is used but all underlying algorithms produce vector layers).

Classify raster into within-field zones. The script performs classification-based zoning of a user-provided raster (e.g., yield, NDVI, or soil property map) within a field boundary polygon. It first buffers the input contour, clips the raster to that buffer, classifies the clipped raster into N classes using Quantiles, Equal-intervals, or K-means, applies modal filtering via GRASS r.neighbors, vectorizes the result, repairs geometries, intersects with the original contour, removes small polygons using GRASS v.clean with a user-defined minimum area threshold, computes zonal statistics (mean and standard deviation) of the original raster per zone, and smooths zone boundaries using GRASS v.generalize with Douglas, Douglas Reduction, or Snakes method. The final output is a vector layer of smoothed, attribute-enriched within-field zones.

Identify flow pathways from DEM. The script identifies flow pathways using a filled DEM and flow accumulation raster via GRASS r.stream.extract, applies a user-defined area threshold (converted from hectares to pixel count), generates flow direction and Strahler order rasters using GRASS r.stream.order, converts the Strahler raster to vector, filters short stream segments (≥3 m), joins Strahler order values to the original stream vector, adds a 'StreamType' field initialized to 5, renames 'cat' → 'Strahler', and removes auxiliary fields ('label', 'stream_typ', 'type_code', 'network'). Outputs include a line vector layer with 'Strahler' and 'StreamType' fields, a streams raster, and a flow direction raster.

Estimate detainment bund catchment storage. The script estimates the storage pond volume (in m³), contributing area (in m²), and storage-to-catchment ratio for potential detainment bund (DB) locations using topographic analysis. It first derives watershed boundaries from flow direction and DB pour points via GRASS r.stream.basins; then computes fill depth (difference between filled and original DEM) over each watershed; rasterizes DB IDs and heights; burns DB heights into a modified DEM; fills sinks with SAGA's Wang-Liu algorithm; calculates volumetric storage by multiplying fill depth (adjusted by Z factor) by pixel area; aggregates storage volume and area per DB catchment via zonal statistics; joins attributes to output polygons; smooths geometries; removes auxiliary fields (_sum, value, cat, fid); and sorts final catchments by storage:contributing-area ratio in descending order. Outputs are a vector layer of catchment polygons with attributes DB_ID, Contr_area, Height (m), Volume(m3), Area (m2), Ratio, and an optional raster of catchment depth (fill depth).

Burn cut lines into DEM. The script burns linear cut features (e.g., drainage cuts or ditches) into an input unfilled DEM by buffering the lines, computing minimum elevation values within those buffers via zonal statistics, rasterizing those minima, and merging the result with the original DEM. It then fills sinks in the modified DEM, computes flow accumulation using GRASS r.watershed, and generates a hillshade. Outputs include: (1) OutputNewDEM (cut-burned DEM), (2) OutputFillDEM (filled version), (3) OutputFlowAcc (flow accumulation raster), and (4) OutputHshd (hillshade).

Generate stream reach and catchment layers. The script identifies main stream reaches from an input flow network vector layer using a user-defined numeric field (LimitField) and classification threshold (ClassValue), then rasterizes the selected reaches. It processes D8 flow direction and filled DEM rasters through TauDEM's AreaD8 and StreamNet tools to compute flow accumulation and derive topologically correct stream networks and associated sub-catchments. Outputs are two vector layers: (1) 'Output Stream Reach' — a line layer of stream reaches with original attributes preserved, and (2) 'Output Sub-catchments' — a polygon layer of delineated catchments, dissolved by value, derived from TauDEM's watershed raster output.

Extract flow pathways from accumulation raster. The script extracts stream networks (flow pathways) by thresholding a flow accumulation raster (converted to hectares), binarizing it, thinning the raster using GRASS r.thin, and converting the thinned raster to vector line features. The output is a vector layer of streams where each line represents an approximate flow pathway; the script explicitly notes that line direction may be incorrect and that this tool is intended for quick visualization rather than accurate hydrological analysis.

Estimate detainment bund catchments. The script estimates the storage pond volume (in m³), contributing area (in m²), and storage:catchment ratio for potential detainment bunds (DBs) by processing user-provided DB location points, a filled DEM, and a flow direction raster. It iterates over unique Height (m)–Length (m) combinations in the input vector layer; for each combination, it buffers DB locations, derives watershed basins using GRASS r.stream.basins, burns DB heights into a modified DEM, computes fill depth via sink-filling (SAGA fillsinksxxlwangliu), calculates volumetric storage per cell (applying Z factor and pixel area), aggregates storage volume and catchment area per DB_ID via zonal statistics, and outputs a dissolved, smoothed, attribute-enriched vector layer of catchments with fields: DB_ID, Contr_area, Height (m), Length (m), Volume(m3), Area (m2), Ratio, and sorted by descending Ratio. An optional depth raster (FillReg) is also generated.

Export contour lines to 3D CAD. The script exports vector contour line layers to a 3D DXF file preserving Z-elevation values. It first checks if the input layer is already 3D (via WKB type >1000); if not, it converts 2D contours to 3D using GRASS v.to.3d with a user-specified numeric elevation field. Then it exports the resulting 3D layer to DXF using QGIS native:dxfexport, respecting target CRS and AutoCAD version compatibility (R2000–R2018). Output is a single .dxf file with 3D geometry and embedded elevation as Z-coordinates.

Calculate Curve Number from land cover and soil data. The script calculates the Soil Conservation Service (SCS) Curve Number (CN) raster for a user-defined polygon study area using two global datasets: ESA WorldCover 2021 (land cover classification) and ORNL HYSOG (hydrologic soil groups). It processes these rasters by clipping to the study area extent, aligning their spatial resolution and extent, performing a pixel-wise lookup using a CSV-based CN table indexed by land cover code and soil group (A/B/C/D → 1/2/3/4), and applying hydrologic condition (Poor/Fair/Good) and antecedent runoff condition (I/II/III) parameters. Outputs include an optional ESA land cover raster, an optional soil group raster, and a mandatory final CN raster clipped to the input polygon. The script also computes and reports mean CN, potential retention (S), and direct runoff (Q) statistics.

Divide parcels by lot width. The script divides input polygon parcels into smaller lots of a specified width (LOT_WIDTH) using geometric division lines derived from shortest polygon sides and oriented minimum bounding boxes for irregular polygons. It identifies regular (rectangular, 5-vertex) polygons directly and computes oriented minimum bounding boxes for irregular ones; then constructs horizontal division lines between midpoints of the two shortest sides, generates perpendicular lot-divider lines spaced at the desired lot width (with optional uniform corner distribution), extends all lines by 5 cm, clips them to the original parcel boundaries, splits the input parcels along those lines, and performs two iterative passes of merging small resulting polygons (below MERGE_THRESHOLD % of average area) based on shared boundary length. The output is a new vector layer of divided parcels with merged small lots.

Watershed basin delineation. The script delineates a watershed basin from a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) and a pour point. It optionally clips an input stream network to the basin. It first resamples the DEM if necessary to reduce its size, then fills sinks using GRASS r.fill.dir, calculates flow direction and accumulation with r.watershed, delineates the watershed with r.water.outlet, converts the raster basin to vector polygon with r.to.vect, smooths the polygon boundary, and finally clips the input stream network if provided. The outputs are a polygon layer of the basin and an optional line layer of the clipped stream network.

Extract and order stream network. The script generates a smoothed stream network vector layer from a digital elevation model (DEM), applying GRASS GIS hydrological tools (r.fill.dir, r.watershed, r.stream.extract) to derive flow direction, accumulation, and streams; then applies QGIS native geometry smoothing; and finally computes Strahler and Shreve stream orders via recursive topological traversal of line features based on upstream/downstream connectivity using start/end point matching and spatial indexing. Outputs include a line feature class with 'Strahler' and 'Shreve' integer attribute fields.

Identify altitude and slope-based environmental zones. The script processes a Digital Elevation Model (DEM/DTM) to generate three vector layers: (1) APP areas above 1800 m elevation, (2) APP areas with slope >45°, and (3) restricted-use areas with slope between 25° and 45°. It reprojects the input DEM to a user-specified projected CRS (e.g., UTM), computes slope in degrees using GDAL’s slope algorithm, applies binary thresholding via LFTools to classify elevation and slope ranges, and converts resulting binary rasters to polygon vector layers by extracting pixels with DN = 1. All outputs are polygon layers with distinct styling applied post-processing.

Convert auxiliary line to polygon. The script converts an input line layer ('Linha_Auxiliar') into a polygon buffer of user-defined width (in meters), reprojects dynamically to the appropriate UTM zone for metric accuracy, intersects the buffered polygon with the 'ATI' (Área Total do Imóvel) polygon layer, fixes geometries, and injects the resulting clipped polygon features directly into a target destination layer—specifically one named starting with 'RIO' or 'SA' (e.g., 'RIO_1', 'SA_2')—within the current QGIS project. The output is not a new layer but an in-place edit: features are added to the selected destination vector polygon layer, with automatic CRS transformation and commit.

Triangular coordinate transformation between D48/GK and D96/TM. The script performs coordinate transformation on vector layers between the Slovenian national coordinate systems D48/GK and D96/TM using a triangular transformation model. It reads transformation parameters from CSV files, applies per-triangle affine transformation to vertices of each input layer, outputs transformed layers to files with appropriate CRS, and optionally fixes geometries and loads result into QGIS project.

Generate noise exposure grid and contours. The script creates a vector grid layer (square cells) over a user-defined extent at a specified resolution, then rasterizes an input vector layer (e.g., noise source or receiver points) using a specified attribute field (e.g., dBA), fills NoData pixels, applies a custom pseudo-color ramp for noise levels (35–80 dB(A)), generates contour lines at a user-defined interval, and produces polygonized isopleths with area calculation (Area_mq). Outputs include: (1) a shapefile of the square grid; (2) a rendered raster layer named 'Raster noise distrubution' with 13 explicit dB(A) color stops; (3) a contour vector layer; and (4) a polygonized isopleth layer with area-in-square-meters attribute.

Cut overlapping surface areas. The script performs geometric operations on surface area polygons stored in a QKan SQLite/SpatiaLite database to resolve overlaps between different surface types (e.g., based on 'abflussparameter'). It creates a temporary table 'temp_flaechencut', computes non-overlapping geometries using ST_Difference and ST_Union, then updates the original 'flaechen' table with cut geometries. Additionally, it generates Voronoi-based catchment areas ('tezg') for selected sewer pipes ('haltungen') by converting pipe centerlines into thin polygons, computing Voronoi skeletons via GRASS v.voronoi.skeleton, clipping to selected subcatchments ('teilgebiete'), and inserting results into the 'tezg' table — all while enforcing topological consistency and validating for intersecting pipes.

Generate basin routing GeoJSON. The script processes basin delineation shapefiles (subbasin polygons, river lines, connected and non-connected lake polygons) to produce GeoJSON routing products. It reprojects layers to WGS84, simplifies geometries with varying tolerances to keep file sizes under 100 MB, calculates new attributes (e.g., 'rvhName'), and exports them as GeoJSON. It then merges selected features (rivers and lakes) into a final 'routing_product_lake_river.geojson' file, handling lake connectivity and attribute cleaning. The workflow is part of a basinmaker toolkit, designed to prepare spatial data for hydrological routing modeling.

Generate grid polygon from NetCDF. The script generates two shapefile outputs from a NetCDF file: (1) Nc_Grids.shp — a point layer where each point represents the centroid of a NetCDF grid cell, with attributes FGID, Row, Col, Gridlon, Gridlat; and (2) Gridncply.shp — a polygon layer where each polygon approximates the boundary of a NetCDF grid cell using bilinear interpolation of corner coordinates derived from adjacent grid nodes (for rotated grids) or axis-aligned averaging (for non-rotated grids), with identical attributes. It also writes Gridcorr.csv containing the same coordinate/ID table. A second function performs area-weighted spatial overlay between two polygon layers (Target_Ply_Path and Mapping_Ply_Path), producing Overlay_Polygons.shp (the dissolved union geometry with computed area field 's_area') and GriddedForcings2.txt (a text file encoding area-proportional mapping weights from mapping-grid polygons to target-HRU polygons). Both functions rely on QGIS processing algorithms via PyQGIS API and netCDF4 for coordinate extraction.

Reproject and clip raster to mask extent. The script reprojects a source raster to match the coordinate reference system and spatial properties (cell size, CRS) of a mask raster, then clips the reprojected raster using a vector mask layer (shapefile). Outputs are two GeoTIFF files: one reprojected ('_proj.tif') and one clipped to the mask geometry ('.tif'), both stored in the GRASS database directory. The workflow uses QGIS Processing algorithms 'gdal:warpreproject' and 'gdal:cliprasterbymasklayer', with no resampling or nodata handling specified, and exits QGIS cleanly after execution.

Process population raster data. The script processes a user-provided population raster by clipping it to individual study area polygons (from a GeoPackage layer named 'study_area_clip_polygons'), expanding each clipped raster to align with the bounding box of its corresponding study area, resampling to a specified cell size using gdalwarp with 'sum' resampling method, reclassifying the resampled rasters into three equal-interval classes based on global min/max population values across all resampled rasters, and generating VRT mosaics for clipped, resampled, and reclassified outputs. Outputs include per-study-area GeoTIFFs at each processing stage and final VRT files: 'clipped_population.vrt', 'resampled_population.vrt', and 'reclassified_population.vrt', plus a QML style file for the reclassified output.

Aggregate GeoE3 scores by subnational boundaries. The script calculates majority-class GeoE3 Score (5 classes: 0–5) and GeoE3 × Population Score (15 classes) for each subnational administrative polygon using zonal statistics (majority mode) on precomputed VRT rasters. It processes up to four raster inputs — 'GeoE3_Score_combined.vrt', 'geoe3_by_population_score.vrt', 'geoe3_score_ghsl_masked.vrt', and 'geoe3_score_by_population_ghsl_masked.vrt' — against a user-provided aggregation vector layer (e.g., provinces or districts). Outputs are GeoPackage layers with columns 'fid', 'name', 'geoe3_score', and 'geoe3_pop_score', styled with QML files ('geoe3_score_vector.qml' and 'geoe3_by_population_vector_score.qml'). Geometry is pre-processed via 'native:fixgeometries' and field-retention to preserve 'fid'.

Process Geospatial Data CRS and Geometry. The script provides utility functions for geospatial data processing in QGIS. It assigns CRS to raster layers using gdal:assignprojection and to vector layers using native:assignprojection. It subsets vector layers by intersecting with a given geometry using native:extractbyextent. It converts a QgsGeometry to a memory vector layer. It fixes geometries with native:fixgeometries and reprojects layers to a target CRS with native:reprojectlayer if needed. It combines multiple rasters into a VRT file via gdal:buildvirtualraster and optionally copies a QML style. The outputs are processed layers returned to the caller.

Calculate multi-buffer travel distances to points of interest. The script calculates concentric isochrone buffers (travel time or distance) around points of interest using OpenRouteService (ORS) API, processes them in subsets due to ORS request limits (max 5 features per call), merges and difference-creates non-overlapping bands, assigns Likert-scale scores (1–5) inversely proportional to buffer distance thresholds, rasterizes the scored bands, and outputs georeferenced TIFFs scaled to the likert scale; results are combined into a VRT and added to QGIS. Inputs include a study area polygon, a vector layer of points (e.g., health facilities, schools), travel mode (Walking/Driving), measurement unit (Distance/Time), and user-defined distance/time thresholds.

Reclassify environmental hazard raster. The script reclassifies an input environmental hazards raster (e.g., fire, flood, landslide, cyclone, or drought) into a standardized 0–5 severity scale using layer-specific threshold rules. It loads the raster via QgsRasterLayer, applies QGIS native 'reclassifybytable' with predefined min/max/value triplets per hazard type, clips the result to the study area’s mask layer, and saves the output as a GeoTIFF (e.g., 'fire_reclassified_0.tif') in the workflow directory. The reclassification logic is hardcoded per layer_id and uses range boundaries (e.g., 2 for landslide, 0 otherwise), and logging confirms rule application and file output.

Generate Vienna DSM mosaic. The script downloads, unzips, reprojects (EPSG:31256 → EPSG:4326), and merges 96 individual DSM GeoTIFF files from the City of Vienna's official open data portal (ma41.geodaten.dom_tif) into a single merged GeoTIFF raster named 'dsm.tif'. The input files follow a grid naming convention (e.g., '22_4_dom_tif.zip') covering Vienna’s administrative area; all outputs are stored in local QGIS temporary paths and registered as a QGIS raster layer with EPSG:4326.

Download and mosaic Vienna DTM. The script downloads Digital Terrain Model (DTM) GeoTIFF files for 104 specific grid regions (e.g., '22_4', '32_2') from the official Vienna city portal (wien.gv.at/ma41), unzips them, reprojects each from EPSG:31256 (MGI / Austria Lambert) to EPSG:4326 (WGS84), and merges all into a single georeferenced raster file dtm.tif. The final merged raster is registered as a QGIS raster layer with CRS 4326.

Download and reproject Vienna orthophotos. The script downloads 84 individual orthophoto ZIP files from the official Vienna city portal (ma41), unzips them, reprojects each TIFF from EPSG:31256 (MGI / Austria Lambert) to EPSG:4326 (WGS84), merges all reprojected TIFFs into a single ortho.jpg raster, and updates the QGIS project with this merged orthophoto layer. All operations are hardcoded for Vienna's administrative grid tiles (e.g., '22_4', '32_2'), and file paths are fixed to local macOS user directory '/Users/arthurrufhosangdacosta/qgis_data/temp/ortho/'. The final output is a georeferenced, globally aligned orthophoto mosaic of Vienna.

Generate 3D city model from DSM and footprints. The script generates a 3D city model in QGIS by extruding building footprints using heights derived from a digital surface model (DSM). It uses various zonal statistics or raster sampling methods (GRASS, SAGA, QGIS native) to compute building heights and assigns them to footprint features. It then applies 3D polygon symbols with extrusion height from the computed attribute, sets up phong material colors, and adds additional layers (streets, trees, water) to the QGIS project. Output layers can be saved to user-specified file paths.

Generate cross-section sample frames. The script generates sample frame polygons by splitting a polygon layer with cross-section lines. It extends the cross‑section lines by a tiny distance (0.000001) to guarantee intersection, splits the polygon into multiple parts using the extended lines, and writes each resulting polygon to an output vector layer. Each feature is assigned a sample_frame_id and a sequential display_label, producing a set of frames suitable for further sampling or analysis within a QGIS processing task.

Earthworks Cut and Fill Grading. The script modifies a DEM by carving and filling based on a platform vector layer with specified absolute level and cut/fill slopes. It creates multi-ring buffers at distance 1 for 100 rings, adds fields for platform level, cut slope, fill slope, then computes cut_level and fill_level for each ring. It rasterizes these levels, and combines with the original DEM using a min-max operation to enforce cut and fill design, producing a graded terrain DEM.

Create LRS marks along road axis. The script takes an input line vector layer (road axis), generates points every 25 meters using the 'Points along geometry' algorithm, and applies a QML style to create visual LRS marks and labels for 25m and 100m intervals. The output is a point vector layer.

Reservoir Flooding Simulation. The script creates a dam on an existing DEM and calculates the flooded area. It first generates a multi-ring buffer around the dam vector layer, computing fill levels for each ring based on the dam top level and wall slope. The buffered layer is rasterized with the fill level values and merged with the original DEM using a conditional raster calculation, resulting in a new DEM with the dam structure. Then, using a seed point inside the reservoir and a specified water level (dam top minus water depth), the GRASS r.lake tool determines the inundated area and produces a lake raster. Outputs include the modified DEM with dam and the lake raster (water depth).

Estimate dam removal reservoir volume. This script provides a QGIS pre-processing widget for dam removal and reservoir estimation. It guides the user to digitize a dam area polygon, estimate the reservoir shape using a negative buffer technique based on dam height and side slope, and then simulate the dam removal by creating a channel and merging the modified terrain raster with the original DEM. Additionally, it includes a raster unit converter. The outputs include a new DEM raster representing the terrain after dam removal and a text summary of the estimated reservoir area and volume.

OSM land use classification. The script processes OpenStreetMap (OSM) landuse raster data to produce a classified landuse vector layer for FLO-2D modeling. It extracts land use classes from a multi-band OSM raster using band value thresholds, combines binary class rasters through raster calculator operations, and then vectorizes the resulting raster, clipping it to a provided grid layer. The output is a vector landuse map with landuse codes ('DN' field).

Merge Italian Cadastral GML Datasets. The script downloads Italian cadastral GML data from the Agenzia delle Entrate WFS for selected provinces and municipalities, extracts map (MAP) and parcel (PLE) files, merges them into single GPKG files, optionally adds derived attribute fields (foglio, particella, sezione_censuaria, comune), reprojects to a target CRS, and loads the output layers into QGIS.

QGIS workflow: Format conversion, Projection. This workflow contains 28 core geospatial operations, including Format conversion, Projection, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Vector spatial analysis. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

Modify land cover using vector field. The script modifies a land cover raster by replacing pixel values within polygons using a numeric attribute field from a vector layer. It first copies the original raster via clip by extent to preserve the original, then runs GDAL rasterize overwrite to burn the field values into the raster, producing a modified land cover raster.

Modify Land Cover by Name. This QGIS algorithm modifies a land cover raster by changing pixel values to a new land cover code in areas defined by a polygon vector layer. It uses a lookup table mapping land cover names to codes, copies the original raster with cliprasterbyextent, then rasterizes the polygons with the selected code to overwrite the raster. The output is a modified land cover raster.

Modify Land Cover by NLCD or C-CAP. The script modifies a land cover raster by replacing pixel values within user-defined polygon areas with a selected NLCD or C-CAP land cover class value. It copies the input raster, then rasterizes the vector overlay using the chosen class code, effectively overwriting areas of interest.

Calculate material transport accumulation. The script provides utility functions for QGIS-based sediment or pollutant transport modeling within the QNSPECT plugin. The key functionality, `grass_material_transport`, uses GRASS `r.watershed` to compute flow accumulation from an elevation raster and a weight raster (representing material to transport) with an option for multiple flow direction. It then replaces no-data values and applies a raster math correction to restore original no-data cells, returning a material transport accumulation raster. Additional utilities manage QGIS layer styling, group organization, matrix filtering, and GDAL raster calculator wrapping to support the transport workflow.

Rasterize soil HSG and K-factor. The script converts a vector polygon soil layer into Hydrologic Soil Group (HSG) and/or K-Factor rasters. It validates that HSG field values are among the allowed categories (A, B, C, D, A/D, B/D, C/D, W, Null). If a K-Factor field is specified, it rasterizes that field using GDAL rasterize with a given cell size. If an HSG field is provided, it first maps the string HSG codes to numeric values via a field calculator expression, then rasterizes the result. Both outputs are single-band rasters with user-defined cell size and extents matching the input layer.

Remove small polygons and holes. The script removes small polygonal objects and holes from a polygon vector layer. It first selects features based on a specified field value, then removes polygons with area below a minimum threshold, and finally deletes holes smaller than a given area, outputting a cleaned vector layer.

Generate DSM and Land Cover from LiDAR. The script processes Swedish national LiDAR point cloud (class 2 ground, class 1 building) together with a building footprint vector layer to produce a digital elevation model (dem.tif), digital surface model (dsm.tif), canopy height model (cdsm.tif), land cover classification (lc.tif: paved, building, deciduous forest, grass, and optionally water from OSM), and leaf area index (lai_10m.tif). It clips the LiDAR, extracts ground and building points, generates DEM/DSM/CDSM using FUSION CanopyModel and GridSurfaceCreate, derives land cover from intensity thresholding and building/vegetation masks, and estimates LAI from return density ratios.

Road network intersection extraction and routing. The script initializes a network from a linestring layer, extracts intersections by dissolving the network, finding line intersections, and removing duplicates. It then provides a routing method that builds a directed graph using QgsVectorLayerDirector and computes the shortest path between two points via Dijkstra's algorithm. Outputs include intersection geometries and the vertex points along the calculated shortest path.

Clip linear network to trajectory buffer. The script clips a given linear network (e.g., roads or paths) to the vicinity of a trajectory (point layer) by converting the trajectory points to a path, buffering that path with a user-specified radius, and then clipping the network to the buffer area. The resulting clipped network is split into single-part features. This QGIS processing algorithm is intended as a preprocessing step for offline map matching, reducing the network to the relevant area around a trajectory.

Clean building polygons and generate Voronoi diagram. The script processes a polygon building layer by deleting holes, removing null geometries, converting multipart to singleparts, and eliminating features with duplicate centroids. It then generates a Voronoi diagram from building centroids, clipped to a 50-meter buffer around the buildings, and saves the cleaned building layer and the Voronoi polygons into a GeoPackage.

Generate hexagon and Voronoi building density maps. The script generates hexagon tessellations and Voronoi polygons from an input vector layer of centroids (e.g., building points) for visualization. It computes spatial aggregations by hexagon grid at varying spacings, filtering hexagons intersecting the original layer, assigning nearest 'osm_id', and summarizing numeric attributes and count of buildings per hexagon. It also creates Voronoi polygons clipped to a buffer around the input layer. Outputs are saved as GeoPackage layers, and layers are added to the project.

OSM Sidewalk Creation Utility Functions. The script provides a collection of reusable PyQGIS functions to support an OSM sidewalk creation workflow. It includes functions for spatial operations (buffering, clipping, intersects, dissolves, polygonize), geometry processing (line splitting, point angle calculations, vertex selection), attribute manipulation (field creation, area/perimeter calculation), spatial indexing, and coordinate transformations to local Transverse Mercator projection. These functions prepare street network data, generate sidewalk polygons, handle spatial relations, and manage layer outputs for the main sidewalk generation algorithm.

Clip and buffer river hierarchy levels. The script is a QGIS plugin that clips an input vector layer using a clip boundary, then separates the clipped hydrological network by three hierarchy levels (Principal, Secondary, Tertiary), assigns distinct colors, creates buffer zones of 100m, 50m, and 20m respectively, and adds all resulting layers to the QGIS project.

Collect natural resource data from feature server. The script loads natural resource data from a Queensland government feature server for user-specified property extents. It supports search by lotplan (using property layer bounding boxes) or direct extent string. It retrieves features in batches, applies a zero-distance buffer for geometry cleaning, clips to property polygons, merges results, saves as a GeoPackage, and adds styled layers to the QGIS canvas.

Extract and merge FiC flood extents. The script extracts flood extent polygons from the FloodsInCanada (FiC) database for a given area of interest and date range. It loads the FiC polygon feature class, selects features using a date expression, clips them to the AOI, dissolves overlapping polygons, and exports a merged, cleaned vector layer. The outputs include intermediate raw selections and final dissolved inundation polygon files.

Extract Raster Values for Field Polygon. The script extracts raster values at point locations generated within an agricultural field polygon, optionally applying an internal buffer. It clips each input raster to the polygon extent, creates a point grid matching the first raster's resolution, clips the grid to the buffered polygon, then samples all raster bands at those points. Column names are derived from raster file names, and multi-band rasters are handled with band suffixes. The final merged attribute table is exported as a GeoPackage point layer and a CSV file, both automatically loaded into the QGIS project.

Compute DTM slope raster. The script processes a digital terrain model (DTM) raster to produce a slope map expressed as percent slope. It first clips the DTM to a user-specified extent and resamples to an output cell size using GDAL Translate. Then it computes slope in degrees using QGIS native slope algorithm. Next, it warps the slope raster with mode resampling to match the output cell size and extent. Finally, using a raster calculator expression, it converts slope from degrees to percent via 100*tan(angle*pi/180) and clips values to a user-defined lower and upper limit, outputting the resulting slope raster.

Evaluate Rasterization Quality. The algorithm evaluates the quality of the rasterization process by comparing vector polygon areas with their rasterized counterparts. It takes a source vector layer and a mask vector layer, rasterizes both using a specified burn field and cell size, clips vector areas to the mask, computes area sums per category, then calculates the masked raster area per value, and finally joins the two tables to compute squared error and combined RMSE, producing a quality index as a percentage of the mask area.

Clip landcover raster to point buffers. The script clips a landcover raster to 1000-meter buffers around each point in a vector point layer. For each feature in the point layer, it extracts the point by its feature ID, creates a buffer of 1000 meters, checks if the buffer intersects the raster extent, and if so, clips the raster using the buffer as a mask, saving the clipped raster as a PNG image in the user's Documents folder.

Address point density grid calculation. The script creates a grid overlay over an address point layer ('punkty_adresowe.gpkg'), counts the number of points within each grid cell, and visualizes the resulting polygon layer with point counts. The grid is created from the point layer's extent buffered by 100 map units, with dimensions 21 columns by 30 rows, resulting in a point density map.

Generate elevation profile from DEM. The script generates an elevation profile along a specified line using a DEM raster. It creates points along the line at a given distance interval (100 meters), samples the raster value at each point, extracts distances and elevation values, and plots the profile.

Analyze slope position distributions. The script computes terrain slope position attributes (slope height, valley depth, normalized height, standardized height, midslope position) from a DEM using the SAGA 'Relative Heights and Slope Positions' algorithm, generates 1000 random sample points within the raster extent, extracts the attribute values at those points, and plots kernel density estimates for each derived variable. Outputs include a vector layer with sampled raster values and KDE distribution plots.

Generate transit walksheds by route. The script generates walking-distance service areas (walksheds) around transit stops by route using a pedestrian network. It buffers stops, clips the network, splits lines, computes service areas, derives convex and concave hulls, and dissolves polygons by route. Processing is done in fixed-size batches to manage memory, with intermediate and final outputs saved as GeoPackages.

Classify interior exterior zones from roads. The script classifies areas as interior or exterior relative to a 12.5-unit buffer around road features (RVFundamental.gpkg) within a reference area (RPFGC_PPSM.gpkg). It buffers the road layer, clips the buffer to the reference area to get the interior zone, computes the difference to get the exterior zone, and merges both into a single output layer of interior and exterior zones.

Generate interior-exterior buffer zones. The script buffers a vector layer (RVFundamental.gpkg) by 12.5 units, clips the buffer with another polygon layer (RPFGC_PPSM.gpkg) to get the interior intersection, computes the difference to get the exterior (non-overlapping) part, and merges both into a single output layer (faixasIntExt.gpkg).

Create interior-exterior buffer strips. The script performs vector geoprocessing to delineate interior and exterior buffer zones. It applies a 20-meter buffer to the RVFundamental layer, clips the buffer with the RPFGC_PPSM boundary layer to define interior zones, uses difference to obtain exterior zones, and merges both into a single output layer. The final layer is added to the QGIS map canvas.

Filter structures near rivers and roads. The script filters and relocates point-based 'structures' by computing line intersections between 'cours_eau' (rivers) and 'routes' (roads), merging those intersections with the original structures, buffering the merged points by 50 meters, dissolving overlapping buffers, computing centroids of the dissolved polygons, and finally extracting only those centroids within 100 meters of the 'cours_eau' layer. The output is a new point vector layer ('New_structures') containing filtered and spatially adjusted structure locations that are both proximal to road-river intersections and near rivers.

Calculate river obstruction indicator F2. The script computes the F2 indicator for each river network segment by measuring the mean unrestricted distance from the river to the first anthropic obstacle, based on normal transects and land use reclassification. It first buffers the river network, clips the landuse raster to the buffer, reclassifies it into three anthropic classes (300, 360, 1), and vectorizes the raster. For each river segment, it generates points along the segment, determines the segment’s mean width via nearest neighbor lookup in a point reference layer, constructs normal transects to both sides, computes the distance to the nearest anthropic feature from the transect endpoints, calculates the mean unobstructed length, and maps it to an integer score (5, 3, 2, or 0). The output adds the 'Indice F2' field to the input river network layer.

Compute river fragmentation index F3. The script calculates the F3 indicator for river network segments to assess watercourse fragmentation by anthropogenic pressures and land use. For each river segment, it splits into equal-length subsegments, creates single-sided buffers, intersects with provided anthropogenic vector layers and reclassified land use polygons, and then computes an index (0, 2, 3, or 5) based on the proportion of unobstructed subsegments. The output is a vector layer with appended 'Indice F3' field.

Compute canopy height from GEDI and terrain rasters. The script computes canopy height as the difference between a canopy elevation raster and a ground elevation raster, clamping negative values to zero. It then merges the resulting canopy height raster with an optional GEDI input raster (likely for co-location or validation), and converts the merged raster pixels to vector points with elevation/height values stored in the 'VALUE' field. The output is a point vector layer (GeoPackage) containing spatialized height measurements.

Clean land cover polygons. The script performs vector geometry cleaning on an input vector layer by sequentially applying geometry repair, polygon dissolution, multipart-to-singlepart conversion, hole removal (for holes < 20 m²), topology-preserving simplification (with user-defined tolerance in meters), and iterative smoothing (with user-defined iterations and offset). The output is a cleaned, simplified, and smoothed single-part polygon vector layer with topological integrity preserved and small artifacts removed.

Save URock wind model outputs. The script post-processes and saves output data from the URock wind model. It computes horizontal wind speed, wind direction, and vertical wind speed from 3D wind components (u, v, w) at specified heights, creates point vector layers (GeoJSON, SHP, FGB) and raster grids (GeoTIFF) for each output height level, optionally generates a NetCDF file with the full 3D wind field and vertical wind profile, and applies building footprint masks to set wind speed to zero inside buildings during vector-to-raster interpolation. It also exports Röckle zone points for building and vegetation regions.

Prepare building and vegetation height layers. The script generates two vector layers: (1) a building footprint layer with an added height attribute (ROOF_HEIGHT by default), computed as the median DSM value within each building polygon (optionally adjusted by subtracting DEM to derive above-ground height); and (2) a vegetation layer either rasterized from a canopy DSM (CDSM) — where polygons are created per rounded height class, dissolved by VALUE, and filtered to exclude 0 m — or derived from point data (trunk locations) via buffering using radius/height fields and aspect ratio (0.75 default) to infer missing attributes, then calculating VEG_HEIGHT. Both outputs are vector files (e.g., .shp, .geojson) with user-specified height field names.

Calculate solar panel coverage area. The script computes the geometric coverage area (as a polygon) of solar panel installations grouped by 'ilot' (island/block), calculates total surface area in hectares, counts full and half tables, and computes a coverage rate (%) as the ratio of total panel area to the enveloping polygon area. It outputs a memory vector layer named 'recouvrement' with attributes: ilot (integer), surface (ha), table (full count), demi_table (half count), and taux (coverage percentage rounded to 1 decimal). The layer is styled with transparent fill, red outline, and labeled with 'taux' values using red text with white halo.

Download and Clip WFS Land Layers. The script downloads WFS vector layers (including ZABAGED and LPIS) configured via a file, gets spatial extent from map canvas or a polygon, fetches layers using bounding box requests, and clips them to the exact extent using QGIS geometry operations. The resulting clipped layers are prepared for further land use/land cover analysis.

Map ATKIS and LBM land cover to Talsim land use. The script maps German national land use/cover datasets (ATKIS Landnutzung and LBM-DE2021) to the Talsim hydrological modeling land use classification system. It performs: (1) for ATKIS: recursive discovery of shapefiles (e.g., 'veg01_f', 'sie02_f') in a user-specified folder, merging them, optional clipping with a polygon layer, dissolving by OBJART_TXT and code fields, then attribute-based mapping using 'atkis_talsim_zuordnung.csv' to assign 'OBJART_NEU' values; (2) for LBM-DE2021: direct mapping of 'LB_AKT' codes with SIE_AKT (surface imperviousness) range conditions using 'lbm_talsim_zuordnung.csv'. Outputs are two GeoPackage layers: 'Landuse' (mapped but undissolved) and 'LanduseDissolved' (dissolved by 'OBJART_NEU', with all other attributes deleted).

Process sub-basin hydrologic parameters. The script processes a user-provided sub-basin polygon layer to compute: (1) maximum and minimum elevation per sub-basin using a DEM via zonal statistics; (2) sub-basin area in hectares; (3) mean imperviousness per sub-basin, either by raster zonal statistics (if imperviousness layer is raster) or by vector intersection + weighted area aggregation (if imperviousness layer is vector); (4) longest flow path (LFP) per sub-basin using WhiteboxTools' LongestFlowpath algorithm on a burn-and-fill preprocessed DEM clipped per sub-basin; (5) LFP rotation (flow direction) relative to south; (6) ZOUT point (outlet) derived as the intersection of the lowest-elevation border sub-basin with the outer boundary of the full sub-basin set. Outputs include: a processed GeoPackage layer with all computed attributes; a GPKG LFP layer; optional SQLite database export conforming to QTalsim schema (with SystemElement and SubBasin tables, WGS84-transformed geometries, and scenario metadata); and optional ASCII-formatted EZG file for Talsim NG4 with fixed-field layout based on a template.

Select tectonic features for node grid. The script selects tectonic line features (ridges, isochrons, subduction zones, passive margins, rifts, cratons, collision zones, hotspots, etc.) from a plate model and polygon layers based on a specified appearance age.
