It first reprojects the input mask layer, constructs a query to a CORINE API, downloads polygons, buffers to fix geometry, reprojects to input CRS, clips to mask, joins a roughness lookup table (containing z0 and d), and outputs a vector layer with land cover IDs, roughness length, and displacement height attributes. The script also enables project snapping settings and applies a style to the output layer.

Extract landcover roughness polygons. The script downloads ESA CCI landcover raster (or GWA4 WorldCover) selected by the user, clips it to a buffered input polygon, polygonizes the raster into a vector layer, and joins it with a roughness lookup table to assign roughness length (z0) and displacement height (d) attributes. The output is a vector polygon layer named 'ESA-CCI landcover polygons', styled for use in WAsP wind energy modeling.

Save WAsP boundary lines. The script saves a 'no attribute' or boundary line layer (LineString geometry) to a WAsP .map file for use in wind resource assessment. It checks that the CRS is not geographic, optionally converts polygons to lines, drops Z values, and splits multiparts. It reads an EPSG-WAsP lookup table to set the projection header, then writes the map file with two fixed points, a scaling factor, and the coordinates of each line feature.

Convert roughness polygons to WEng raster. The script converts roughness polygons (vector with 'z0' attribute) to a raster with given grid spacing and saves it as a WEng .grd file for wind resource assessment. It uses gdal:rasterize to rasterize the polygon layer and gdal:translate to export as .grd. The output is a roughness raster file in WEng format.

Extract GWA elevation contours. The script extracts elevation contour lines from a Global Wind Atlas (GWA) digital elevation model for a user-provided polygon area. It downloads a cloud-optimized GeoTIFF (either SRTM Viewfinder-corrected DEM or Copernicus DEM 30 m) via vsicurl, clips it to the extended bounding box, handles zero elevations by adjusting them to near-zero, and then generates contour lines at a specified interval and offset using GDAL contour. If the terrain variation falls below the interval, it produces a boundary line with the mean elevation. The output is a vector layer with an 'ELEV' attribute, styled for use in WAsP mapping.

Generate roughness map from ESA WorldCover. The script generates a WAsP-compatible roughness map from ESA WorldCover 2020 landcover data. It downloads WorldCover tiles for a user-defined polygon area, merges and clips rasters, resamples to a coarser resolution, polygonizes, and joins a roughness lookup table to assign roughness length (z0) and displacement height (d) attributes. The output is a vector layer with polygons representing landcover classes and their roughness parameters.

Global Curve Number Calculation. The algorithm computes a Curve Number (CN) raster for a study area polygon using ESA WorldCover 2021 (10 m) land cover and ORNL HYSOG tiled hydrologic soil groups. It downloads required soil tiles, fills nodata, reprojects, aligns rasters, applies a CN lookup table based on hydrologic condition and antecedent runoff condition, and clips the result to the study area. Optional outputs are ESA land cover and soil group rasters. Summary statistics include mean CN.

Optimized parcel division. The script implements an optimized parcel division algorithm that processes input polygon features representing land parcels, splitting them into smaller lots based on a desired lot width. It treats rectangular polygons directly and approximates irregular polygons with oriented minimum bounding boxes to compute division lines. It generates horizontal (midline) and perpendicular division lines, clips them to the parcel boundaries, splits polygons, and performs two passes of merging small polygons below a threshold percentage of average area to avoid slivers. The output is a polygon layer of subdivided parcels with the original attributes.

Generate tree planting point patterns. The script generates tree planting points with five spatial patterns (triangular/quincunx, rectangular/square, five of diamonds, keyline, random distribution) inside polygon features. It applies a user-defined border margin, parses a flexible spacing string to determine planting distances, and optionally uses a DEM raster to perform automatic slope analysis, sampling slope values at each point and adding a 'slope' field. For the keyline pattern, it generates contours and stream networks from the DEM. The output is a point vector layer with attributes id, pattern, x, y, and optionally slope, along with a comprehensive report of counts per pattern and planting density per hectare.

Delineate watershed basin and stream order. The script delineates a watershed basin from a DEM and a pour point using GRASS GIS algorithms (r.fill.dir, r.watershed, r.water.outlet, r.to.vect). It smooths the basin boundary and clips an input stream network to the basin. Three Strahler stream order calculations are performed: standard (sthr_original), main channel extension along longest paths (sthr_extend), and extension to all headwaters (sthr_final). The outputs are a watershed basin polygon and a stream line layer containing the three Strahler order fields.

Bathymetric data anisotropic IDW interpolation. The script implements a QGIS plugin for bathymetric data interpolation. It takes point measurements of depth, a centerline vector, and an ROI polygon. It computes S (along-stream) and N (cross-stream) coordinates and flow direction for each point. Then, it generates a regular grid of sample points within the ROI extent and interpolates depth values using an anisotropic Inverse Distance Weighting (EIDW) method that accounts for anisotropy ratio and max distance. The result is rasterized to a DEM and optionally evaluated with RMSE against original points.

Create bathymetry sampling points grid. This script creates a constant raster grid with user-defined extent and pixel size, then samples one point per pixel in the center using the 'pixelstopoints' algorithm. The sampled points layer is prepared for interpolation by adding fields for S, N, and Interpolated values. Additionally, it converts a raster output to a layer and assigns a nodata value to band 1, intended for post-processing of bathymetric flow DEM outputs.

Raster-point difference RMSE calculation. The script validates a raster surface by comparing it to point measurements using the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). It clips the input point layer to a specified extent, samples raster values at the clipped point locations using the QGIS native raster sampling tool, and aggregates the actual values (from a point attribute field) and predicted values (sampled raster). It then computes the RMSE between the two arrays and prints the mean squared difference and RMSE. The processed point layer with sampled raster values is returned and named 'Data validation - differences'.

Convert vector layers to GPX format. The algorithm converts any vector layer (points, lines, polygons) to a GPX file with tracks. It first fixes geometries, then converts polygons to lines if necessary, dissolves features unless a name field is specified, optionally splits multipart features into single parts, and refactors fields to add a 'name' attribute from a user-defined display name or an attribute field. The output is written using QgsVectorFileWriter with GPX-specific options (FORCE_GPX_TRACKS, GPX_USE_EXTENSIONS). The resulting file is a GPX file suitable for Garmin devices.

Export QGIS data to ur-scape. The script exports an active QGIS layer (raster or vector) to the ur-scape data format by converting it into grid CSV files with metadata, categories, data values and masks. It handles rasterization of vectors, reprojection to EPSG:4326, aggregation of raster cells (weighted average or summary), no-data masking, and special outputs for municipal budget and road network reachability graphs. Output files are location-specific and the script also updates layers.csv to register the layer.

Hexagon binning point count. The script performs hexagonal binning on an input point layer using H3 spatial indexing. It projects the layer to geographic coordinates (EPSG:4617), generates hexagon grids at user-specified resolution covering the layer's extent, counts points within each hexagon, writes shapefiles with a 'numpoints' field, and applies graduated color symbology. The output hexagon layers are added to the QGIS project.

Geotagged photo import and 360° viewer. The script provides a QGIS plugin to import geotagged photos into a GeoPackage point layer, extract EXIF metadata (timestamps, azimuth), add custom attributes from filename patterns (road number, street, section, mileage), and launch a 360° equirectangular image viewer docked in QGIS for selected features. Workflow includes creating/updating GeoPackage, removing duplicates, and interactive map selection tools.

View street-level panoramic photos. The script implements a QGIS dockable widget for viewing equirectangular images associated with point features from a vector layer. It loads the image file based on a filename attribute, extracts metadata (timestamp, road name, street name, section name), and uses OpenGL to render the panoramic image with interactive yaw rotation. It updates a map canvas rubber band arrow to indicate viewing direction, computes hotspots by buffering the selected point in EPSG:3857 with mercator compensation, filters adjacent points, and places clickable navigation markers. It supports screenshots and fullscreen toggling, and reprojects coordinates between layer CRS, EPSG:4326, and EPSG:3857 as required.

Clean and Snap Points to Roads. The script processes measurement points and OSM road data. It optionally converts multipart road segments to single parts and removes roads tagged as 'construction' or 'proposed'. Then it snaps the points to the nearest road segment within a user-defined tolerance. The output is a point layer with snapped geometry.

Extract spot heights from DEM. The script identifies local maximum elevation points (spot heights) from a DEM. It first uses a circular neighborhood maximum filter (r.neighbors) to find the maximum elevation in a user-defined neighborhood around each cell. The original DEM is then compared to the neighborhood maximum via raster calculator, retaining only cells where the values are equal (local maxima) and setting others to zero. Zero cells are set to null, and the resulting raster is converted to point features. A coastline polygon extracts onland points. The output is a point layer of spot heights with an elevation attribute.

Disconnected Network Segments. The script identifies topologically connected and disconnected line segments of a river network. Starting from an input river mouth point layer, it iteratively selects vertices that intersect already-selected vertices to propagate connectivity through the network. It then separates the line features into disconnected (no path to river mouth) and connected segments, outputting two vector layers.

Extract Springs. The algorithm extracts headwater springs from a vector line network. It first dissolves the network, identifies dangling vertices (ends), splits dissolved lines at these vertices, extracts line segments intersecting dangling points, calculates their length, filters by user-specified length threshold (minimum, maximum, or all), removes segments intersecting river mouth buffer to exclude false positives, and outputs the filtered headwater lines and corresponding points with original attributes.

Classify pseudo-node connectivity. The script analyzes pseudo-nodes (break points) in an input line layer and classifies them based on their spatial relationship with vertices of user-selected map layers. It first extracts pseudo-nodes via an internal algorithm, then creates a point layer from all vertices of the selected layers, tagging each vertex with its source layer name. Using spatial join operations, it splits the pseudo-nodes into two outputs: a non-overlapping layer containing pseudo-nodes disjoint from all vertices, and an overlapping layer containing pseudo-nodes that intersect one or more vertices, retaining the source layer identifier.

Convert polygons to singlepart lines. The script converts an input polygon layer to a single-part line layer. It first applies 'qgis:polygonstolines' to extract polygon boundaries as lines, then 'qgis:multiparttosingleparts' to split multipart geometries into individual segments. It reassigns a unique integer 'fid' field to each resulting feature and transfers rendering properties (color) from the input layer to the output. The final output is a line layer suitable for further analysis.

Widen Taxiway Lines. The script widens taxiway line features by buffering them with a user-specified distance, optionally dissolving and converting the result to linestrings. It reprojects the input to EPSG:3857, applies buffer, then reprojects back to EPSG:4326.

Calculate Longest Flow Path in Watershed. The script extracts the longest hydrological flow path within a watershed basin. It selects stream channels that intersect the basin, extracts the first vertices of each stream segment, computes a distance matrix to the pour point to identify the farthest vertices, builds a shortest path network from the pour point to these vertices, and selects the path with the maximum travel cost (longest distance). The final output is a line vector layer of the longest stream, with an elongation ratio calculated and saved.

Watershed delineation and curve number. The script delineates the upslope contributing watershed for a given discharge point from a filled DEM using SAGA upslope area algorithm, then processes the vector watershed polygon (fixing geometries, dissolving). It clips the DEM and channel network to the watershed, generates contours, computes watershed statistics (area, perimeter, elevation stats), and calculates Curve Numbers by intersecting the watershed with soil and Corine land cover layers to produce CN map and classification polygons.

shred layer into grid fragments. The script is a QGIS plugin that divides a selected vector or raster layer into a grid of vertical strips, horizontal strips, or rectangular cells, clips the layer to each grid cell, and optionally shuffles the positions of the resulting vector fragments. It then removes the original layer from the project and deletes its file from disk.

Query cadastral parcels from WFS. The script provides functions to interact with the Slovenian e-prostor WFS service for cadastral parcel data. It can load a list of parcel numbers for a given cadastral municipality (KO_ID), retrieve the geometry of a specific parcel and add it as a QGIS layer, select parcels intersecting a user-defined area with optional buffer, and load cadastral municipality codes from WFS or a local CSV file. It also manages layer metadata and flashes geometries on the map canvas.

Create Graphab habitat connectivity project. The script provides a graphical user interface (dialog) for configuring and launching the 'graphab3:create_project' QGIS processing algorithm. It allows users to select a landscape raster (as a file or map layer), define habitat codes by selecting from unique raster values, optionally set patch size and maximum size thresholds, specify nodata value, project name, and output directory. Upon confirmation, it executes the processing algorithm to create a Graphab project for landscape connectivity analysis.

Merge rasterized vectors with custom encoding. The script provides a dialog for rasterizing vector layers and merging them with custom pixel value reclassification. Users add vector and raster layers, define encoding to reassign pixel values, set output resolution and extent, then the tool rasterizes vectors, replaces codes on rasters, splits rasters by code groups, and merges them into a single output raster file. The result is loaded as a new raster layer in QGIS.

Detect and dissect polygon overlaps. The script processes an input polygon layer to detect overlapping features. It first fixes geometries, adds an identification field, performs polygon self-intersection (SAGA) to identify overlapping areas, selects intersecting features, and optionally zooms to overlaps. If 'dissect' option is selected, it extracts the overlapping parts into a new polygon layer named 'Intersected'. If 'dissolve' option is selected, it assigns the overlapping slivers to adjacent polygons based on user-specified criteria (largest adjacent, smallest adjacent, or largest common boundary) and outputs a 'Dissolved' layer.

Area-weighted data comparison by grid. The script calculates area-weighted averages of a data field from a polygon layer intersecting a grid layer. It renames input fields, computes polygon areas, performs an intersection, computes intersection areas, and then calculates a weighted sum grouped by grid cell ID. The result is a grid layer with an area-weighted average attribute.

Select adjacent cell coverage polygons. The QGIS tool allows users to interactively select neighboring polygons from a coverage layer and identify associated point features. It first processes a point layer to generate Voronoi polygons (cell coverage zones), then provides a map tool where clicking a polygon selects all adjacent polygons up to a user-defined depth using spatial touching/intersection analysis. The selected polygons are highlighted with color-coded rubber bands. For the clicked polygon and each neighbor polygon, the tool extracts point features that fall inside them and copies the main point attributes along with each neighbor point's attributes to the system clipboard for external use.

Clean building footprints and generate Voronoi polygons. The script cleans building polygon layers by deleting holes, removing null geometries, converting multipart to singlepart, renumbering duplicate IDs, and removing features with duplicate centroids. It then creates centroid points, generates Voronoi polygons from these centroids, buffers the original buildings, and clips the Voronoi polygons with the buffer. The cleaned buildings and Voronoi layer are saved as a GeoPackage for further accessibility analysis.

Generate hexagon grids with aggregated building attributes. The script generates Voronoi polygons and hexagon grids from an input polygon layer for accessibility visualization. It computes centroids, optionally creates Voronoi diagrams clipped to a buffer, generates hexagon grids at multiple spacings, filters hexagons intersecting the input layer, assigns the nearest source ID from centroids, and aggregates building counts and numeric attribute sums per hexagon. The final dissolved hexagon layers and the Voronoi layer are saved as GeoPackage files and loaded into QGIS.

Create boundary mesh layer. The script creates boundary conditions for a Telemac mesh by validating and processing input mesh, contour polygon, and boundary line/point layers. It checks boundary layer fields and spatial containment, extracts vertices if polygon input is used, runs an external Telemac script to assign boundary values, and outputs updated mesh files (.slf and .cli).

Extend mesh from extended contour. The script extends an existing mesh layer by defining an extended contour and optional other meshes, islands, constraints, and refinement areas. It converts the input Selafin mesh to MED format, runs a SALOME meshing script to extend the mesh using the specified mesh size, growth rate, and engine, then converts the output back to Selafin format.

Geological deposit spatial analysis. The script provides QGIS processing functions for spatial analysis of geological/mineral deposit data. Key methods include select by location and attributes, buffering, difference (ring creation), aggregation of features by geological stage (concatenating attributes like notation, description, era, series, deposit type), centroid extraction, vertex extraction, reprojection, merging and cleaning duplicates, network centrality (degree, closeness, betweenness, eigenvector) using GRASS, node extraction, shortest path (distance and time-based via GRASS), path reconstruction, closest/furthest point identification from polygons. Outputs are temporary vector layers (memory or temp files) for each operation.

Extract high altitude and steep slope areas. The script processes a Digital Terrain Model (MDT) and a property boundary layer to generate vector polygons representing areas with altitude above 1800 meters and slope greater than 45 degrees. It first reprojects the MDT to a projected CRS, then applies binary thresholding to isolate elevations >=1800 m and slope >=45° using the LFTools plugin and native slope calculation. The resulting binary rasters are polygonized and filtered to keep pixels with value 1 (meeting criteria), then clipped to the property boundary. The outputs are two separate layers: one for altitude exceedance and one for slope exceedance, both symbolized with hatch patterns in post-processing.

Auxiliary Line to Water Body Polygon. Converts an auxiliary line layer into a polygon representing a water body or permanent preservation area using a user-defined width, then clips it to the property boundary (ATI). The script reprojects the line to a UTM zone based on the layer centroid, dissolves it, buffers by half the specified width with flat end caps, reprojects back to EPSG:4674 (SIRGAS 2000), intersects with the ATI polygon, cleans geometries, and adds the resulting features to a destination layer starting with 'RIO' or 'SA'.

Create atlas coverage from line. Generates atlas control points and polygon coverage along a line based on paper size, scale, and overlap. Computes real-world dimensions, creates points along the line at regular intervals with a step distance that accounts for map scale and paper long axis minus overlap, and then creates rotated rectangular polygons representing atlas page extents aligned to the line direction. The output point layer includes an 'angle' field for rotation and the polygon layer shows page footprints.

Process DTB raster for excavation impact map. The script processes DTB (Digital Terrain Model) raster data for excavation polygon areas by clipping to expanded extents, resampling to a specified resolution, and converting to TIFF. It also includes utility functions for vector layer JSON conversion, reprojection, file moving, and mapping pore pressure curve names for Norwegian translations in tunnel damage assessment.

Compute distance to features or raster values. This script computes a distance raster from either specified raster cell values or vector features. For raster inputs, it uses gdal:proximity with a list of target pixel values; for vector inputs, it first rasterizes the vector layer to match the reference raster extent and pixel size, then applies proximity. The output is a single-band raster where each cell's value represents the distance to the nearest target cell or feature, in the same units as the raster (if units=1).

Simplify flight plan waypoints. The script simplifies a drone flight plan by reducing the number of waypoints while preserving photo spacing and coverage. It takes a CSV file containing waypoints with longitude, latitude, and altitude, a DEM raster, a projected CRS, and a tolerance value. The algorithm creates 3D points, samples DEM elevations, reprojects, generates a flight line, simplifies the line using the Visvalingam method, extracts vertices, creates buffers, spatially joins with the original points to select waypoints, and outputs a filtered CSV. Optionally, it adds original points, the flight line, and simplified points as map layers.

Slice polygon layers by extruded line volume. The script slices 3D polygon vector layers using a volume defined by a buffered linestring extruded between given Z minimum and Z maximum. It first buffers the input linestring, converts to singlepart, translates to Z minimum, extrudes to Z maximum, then performs solid 3D intersection with each input polygon layer. The results are styled like the source layers and added to a new group in the QGIS project.

Generate stratified sampling polygons. The script provides functionality for creating stratified shapefiles in QGIS. It allows users to manually draw strata boundaries using three methods: freehand lines, polylines (with optional horizontal/vertical constraints), or Voronoi polygons from points. The tool uses a specified sampling area layer as the extent. It polygonizes the drawn lines merged with the boundary, clips to the sampling area, and generates a polygon shapefile with attributes for ID, strata name, and area. The output shapefile contains the delineated strata polygons for subsequent stratified sampling workflows.

Interpolate point precipitation values to raster. The script interpolates point meteorological measurements (e.g., precipitation) to a continuous raster surface using IDW or Nearest Neighbor methods, then converts the resulting raster to a NumPy array for subsequent weighted average raster generation. It leverages QGIS processing algorithms (qgis:idwinterpolation and gdal:gridnearestneighbor) with user-defined extent, cell size, and interpolation parameters.

Merge Italian cadastral map and parcel data. The script merges Italian cadastral GML files (MAP and PLE) downloaded from Agenzia delle Entrate WFS. It filters by province and comune, extracts relevant GML files, merges them into GPKG format, adds calculated fields (foglio, particella, sezione censuaria, comune), optionally reprojects, and loads the layers into QGIS.

Execute GEEST spatial analysis workflow. The WorkflowBase module provides an abstract processing pipeline for the GEEST plugin to assess gender-enabling environments. It loads study area geometries from a GeoPackage, iterates over sub-areas, applies subclass-defined analysis on vector or raster layers per area, masks results with area polygons, and merges per-area outputs into a single VRT file. Other capabilities include coordinate transformation, nodata filling, rasterization of vector layers, and optional GHSL settlement data download and processing.

Generate multi-buffer distance rasters. The script generates multi-buffer isochrones around point locations using road network travel distances. For national and local scales, it employs QGIS native network analysis to create concentric travel-time or travel-distance polygons. For regional scale, it uses a simple buffer approach with percentage intersection scoring. The resulting isochrone layers are scored and rasterized to grid cells, producing accessibility rasters that are combined into a VRT.

Multi-buffer isochrone accessibility scoring. The script computes multi-buffer travel time/distance isochrones from OpenRouteService for user-provided points of interest, dissolves overlapping areas to create non-overlapping bands, assigns inverted accessibility scores, and rasterizes the result to produce a suitability layer for gender enabling environment analysis.

Environmental hazard reclassification. This script reclassifies environmental hazard rasters (landslide, fire, flood, cyclone, drought) into a 0-5 scale based on predefined rules specific to each hazard type. It applies reclassification by table using QGIS processing, then clips the result to the study area mask. Outputs are reclassified raster files per area in GeoTIFF format.

Geospatial data preprocessing for GEEST plugin. This script provides utility functions for the GEEST plugin to assign coordinate reference systems (CRS) to raster and vector layers, subset vector layers by area of interest, fix geometries, reproject layers, and combine multiple rasters into a virtual raster (VRT) file for subsequent analysis. It serves as a preprocessing module for gender enabling environments spatial assessment.

Reclassify population raster to three classes. The script clips a population density raster to study area masks using GDAL cliprasterbymasklayer, resamples each clipped raster to a specified cell size with gdalwarp sum aggregation, reclassifies the resampled values into three classes based on the global minimum and maximum across all resampled rasters (native:reclassifybytable), and finally creates VRT files combining clipped, resampled, and reclassified rasters. The reclassified raster is styled with a three-class QML. This task is part of the GEEST QGIS plugin to support gender-enabling environment analysis.

Subnational Gender Enablement Score Aggregation. The script aggregates gender enablement environment (GeoE3) scores and GeoE3 x Population scores to subnational boundary polygons. It reads precomputed VRT rasters for each score type (including optional GHSL masked variants), fixes geometry of the aggregation layer, and uses QGIS native zonal statistics to compute the majority score class per polygon. The output geopackages contain polygons with aggregated score attributes, and corresponding QML style files are applied for visualization.

Create Depth Raster from XYZ. The script converts one or more XYZ text files containing Easting, Northing, and Depth data into raster layers. It supports multiple file processing, auto-detects grid size per file, and offers direct rasterization or IDW interpolation. The output is GeoTIFF rasters with depth values, optionally compressed, added to the QGIS project.

Merge MBES Depth Rasters. Merge Multibeam Echo Sounder (MBES) raster layers into a single seamless raster using GDAL merge, preserving original depth values and correctly handling NoData values for transparency. The process optionally applies LZW compression to reduce file size. The output is a merged raster file containing continuous bathymetric data.

Create Rockyfor3D Input Rasters. The script prepares input rasters for the Rockyfor3D rockfall simulation model by rasterizing selected numeric vector field attributes onto a grid matching a provided DEM. It ensures data alignment with the DEM's resolution and extent, converts to ASCII format, renames specific fields to match model requirements (e.g., rockdensit to rockdensity, conif_perc to conif_percent), and validates field type and value constraints. The outputs are ASCII raster files for each field, optionally loaded into QGIS.

Download Warsaw cadastral boundaries. The script downloads cadastral vector data (parcels and buildings) for specified districts of Warsaw from a municipal server via HTTP requests, extracts shapefiles from ZIP archives, and loads them into the QGIS project. It merges all district data into a single layer or adds separate layers, assigns the Polish coordinate system EPSG:2178, and adjusts the map canvas extent. Network errors are logged, and temporary files are cleaned up.

Generate contours and hillshade. The script generates fine contour lines and hillshade shading from a DEM raster clipped to the current map canvas extent. It first clips the DEM using GDAL Clip Raster by Extent, optionally creates a hillshade layer with GDAL hillshade using user-specified azimuth and altitude, then generates contour lines at a fine step interval. It identifies coarse contours by checking if elevation is near multiples of the wide step using a ratio threshold, assigns a 'coarse' attribute, applies a predefined style, and optionally fixes contour altitude masking. The resulting contour and hillshade layers are added to the map.

Extract polygon edge strips. The script extracts edges from polygon geometries in a vector layer. It processes input polygons by converting to single parts, fixing geometries, simplifying to tenths of millimeter tolerance, then buffers inward and outward by half the specified width, computes the difference between the outer and inner buffers, dissolves the resulting strips, fixes geometries, adds a field 'h' with a value from braille.DIM['f'], and outputs the final polygon layer representing the edge strips.

Package Multiple GIS Layers to KMZ. The script is a QGIS processing algorithm that packages multiple vector and raster layers into a single KMZ file. It first takes input layers, optionally reprojects them to a target CRS, and optionally preserves layer styles. Then it processes each layer: vector layers are exported to KML using QgsVectorFileWriter, while raster layers are reprojected and converted to KML using GDAL tools (gdal:warpreproject and gdal:translate with KMLSUPEROVERLAY). Finally, all KML files are combined into a ZIP archive (KMZ) with a master KML document. The output is a KMZ file containing all selected layers.

Download Top10NL topographic features. The script is a QGIS plugin that downloads selected Top10NL topographic feature layers from the PDOK OGC API Features service using GDAL's convertformat with a user-specified extent, saving them into a GeoPackage file. It also performs deduplication of features by 'ID' attribute when appending, logs processing steps, and optionally adds the layers to the current QGIS project.

Create water network listening zones. The script generates listening zones (zones d'écoute) around manually or layer-based points along a water pipe network. It first densifies line geometries at 1-unit intervals, then for each start point finds the nearest line and computes a travel cost based on the line's material (MATERIAU) and diameter (DIAMETRE) using a detailed lookup table. Using QGIS network analysis (service area from layer), it computes a service area with the travel cost, buffers the result by 1 meter, and merges all individual zones into a single output layer named 'Zones d'écoute'.

Generate drone flight restriction zones. The script generates drone flight restriction zones around airfields and helipads by creating concentric buffer rings with varying radii corresponding to height restrictions (e.g., FRZ, ≤100ft, ≤200ft, ≤300ft, ≤400ft). For airfields, it processes a selected runway line feature, buffers the runway, creates lateral and head line features, and uses a sector at each runway end to split restriction zones into 'lado' (side) and 'cabeceira' (head) regions. For helipads, it creates simple concentric rings around a selected point. The outputs are styled polygon layers added to the QGIS map.

Create lateral buffers from lines. This QGIS plugin creates lateral buffers on both sides of selected line features from the active layer. Using user-specified offset and buffer distances, it first runs the array offset algorithm to generate left (negative offset) and right (positive offset) parallel lines, removes any zero-offset features, then creates single-sided buffers on each side (left buffer with side=1, right buffer with side=0). The left and right buffers are merged into a single memory layer and added to the map.

Download BGT topography features. The script downloads selected BGT topographic features (e.g., roads, buildings, water) from the PDOK OGC API Features service within a user-specified bounding box, saves them to a GeoPackage file, and optionally loads them into QGIS. It uses the GDAL OGR vector conversion tool to fetch features via OAPIF, deduplicates appended layers by attribute, and logs progress.

Design sewer network layout. The script designs a sewer network layout by extracting street centerlines, clipping them to a study area, snapping an outlet point, creating a minimum spanning tree from shortest paths, and correcting flow directions and invert elevations to ensure proper gravitational drainage. It processes vector street data and a digital elevation model, producing sewer pipe and node layers with corrected elevation attributes.

Prepare urban drainage design inputs. The script prepares input data for urban drainage system design. It processes building and street data to compute contributing areas, slopes, imperviousness, and connections to sewer nodes. It uses a DEM to derive slopes, determines pipe lengths and slopes, and aggregates subcatchments with population data for combined sewer systems. The outputs are CSV design files for nodes, pipes, and subcatchments.

Rank and merge skipped pipe links. The script processes street/pipeline network layers to correct node elevations and calculate elevation differences, then adds aggregated flow (Q) and diameter data from tabular dataframes. It ranks links based on a weighted score of normalized length and flow, prioritizing non-head nodes. Finally, it merges a percentage of top-ranked previously skipped links into a designed network layer, retaining only essential fields such as LINK_ID, length, FROM_NODE, TO_NODE, slope, and Diameter.

Sentinel-2 Cloud Masking with Shadow Detection. This script is a QGIS plugin that applies cloud masking to Sentinel-2 Level-1C imagery using the enhanced s2cloudless algorithm with adaptive thresholding and cloud shadow detection. It reads Sentinel-2 band files from a local product directory, reprojects them to a user-defined CRS, and crops to the current map canvas extent. The bands (B01–B12) are stacked, and the S2PixelCloudDetector is used to generate an initial cloud mask. Additionally, the Bare Soil Index (BSI) is calculated to create a bare soil mask that aids in identifying cloud shadows; the combined mask is then refined with averaging and binary dilation. The final binary mask is saved as a GeoTIFF, and masked versions of 10m/20m bands (B02, B03, B04, B05, B06, B07, B08, B8A, B11, B12) are produced for further analysis.

Mask and mosaic Sentinel-2 L1C imagery. The plugin downloads Sentinel-2 L1C imagery over the current map canvas extent from Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem, applies cloud masking using s2cloudless, and optionally creates a median composite mosaic from multiple dates. It outputs cloud-masked multi-band GeoTIFF files and true color image (TCI) previews.

Batch export map tiles and elevation rasters. The script batch-exports atlas map tiles from a QGIS layout as GeoTIFF images and generates corresponding masked elevation rasters. It uses a user-provided DEM and a coverage grid layer. For each atlas feature, it exports the layout to a high-resolution GeoTIFF, then creates a mask raster from the grid layer with identical extent and resolution, warps the DEM to that extent, and applies the mask to clip the DEM, writing the result. The process is logged.

Delineate watersheds and stream networks. The script generates catchments, streams, and stream networks from a DEM. It fills sinks, computes flow accumulation and watershed basins, extracts streams based on a user-defined threshold, smooths stream geometry, generalizes catchments using GRASS v.generalize with snakes method, calculates both Strahler and Shreve stream orders, joins catchments with stream network attributes, and dissolves catchments to create network polygons. Outputs are three styled vector layers: streams (graduated by Shreve order with Viridis ramp), catchments (categorized by network with random colors), and networks (blue outlines with labels).

Identify Ponds from DEM. This QGIS processing script identifies ponds (sinks) in a ground raster (DEM) by filling sinks, computing pond depth as the difference between filled and original DEM, filtering by minimum depth and area, and polygonizing the valid pond extents. It then performs zonal statistics to assign attributes such as maximum and minimum elevation, pond volume, and depth statistics to each pond polygon. The outputs include a vector layer of pond outlines with attached attributes, and optionally the filled DEM and pond depth rasters.

e-Stat mesh batch import merge secret values. This QGIS algorithm batch-imports e-Stat regional mesh statistics from ZIP files, cleans and renames fields using Japanese metadata rows, normalizes mesh codes, handles secret-treated values by merging them into designated group codes, auto-generates mesh polygon geometries (1km/500m/250m) using mesh code to bounding box conversion, dissolves polygons by group ID, sums numeric fields, adds source row counts (SRC_COUNT), and optionally extracts meshes intersecting administrative boundary polygons. Outputs integrated mesh polygon layers with merged statistics.

Classify flood depth raster. The script generates a classified flood depth raster from an input water depth raster and user-defined class breakpoints. It first sorts the breakpoints, constructs a r.mapcalc expression that sums binary condition layers (A > class_i) to assign integer classes, then applies a sieve filter to remove small polygons from the resulting raster. Output is a classified raster where pixel values indicate the highest class threshold that the water depth exceeds.

Vectorize water depth classes. This script vectorizes water depth classes from a water depth raster. It uses a user-specified list of threshold values (in metres) and for each threshold, generates a binary raster indicating areas where water depth exceeds that value. The processing steps include raster algebra (A>B), null value conversion, sieve filtering to remove small areas, raster to vector conversion, geometry fixing, dissolving, and attribute field creation with the threshold value. The resulting polygon layers for all thresholds are merged into a single vector output, each feature attributed with its depth class.

Interpolate high water marks. The script interpolates a vector layer containing high water marks (CPHE) to create a raster surface. It supports multiple interpolation methods: regularized spline with tension (v.surf.rst), bilinear, bicubic, and stepped (Voronoi polygon-based). If a mask is provided, processing is performed per zone, and results are merged. The workflow includes optional centroid calculation, buffering, rasterization, and optional projection onto a DTM if provided. The output is a raster of interpolated CPHE values.

Delete isolated flood polygons. The script removes isolated flood extent polygons that do not overlap a reference overlay layer within a specified distance tolerance. It dissolves the input polygon layer, buffers the overlay layer, selects input polygons intersecting the buffer, and clips the original input to these selected polygons, producing a cleaned vector layer.

Cut disk geometries into rings. This QGIS processing algorithm converts concentric disk polygons (e.g., flooded area extents at different water levels) into annuli by dissolving, splitting, and sorting features based on a user-selected attribute field. It then computes the geometric difference between pairs of consecutive layers using native:difference, and merges the resulting rings into a single polygon layer. Optionally, it removes an automatically created 'fid' column if it was not present in the original input.

Compute flood depth above minimum height. The algorithm projects a high water level raster (CPHE) onto a digital terrain model (MNT) to compute water depths. It subtracts the terrain from the water surface, then extracts areas where the resulting depth exceeds a user-specified minimum height threshold. The output is a raster of heights above the minimum threshold, representing flood depths.

Refine height class polygons. The script refines vector polygons representing height classes (elevation zones) using a buffer-based refinement strategy. It applies a sequence of positive and/or negative buffers, group-by-field dissolve, simplification, small area/hole removal, and smoothing. The output is a cleaned and smoothed polygon layer.

Assemble flood rings into disks. The script assembles polygon ring geometries (e.g., flood extent rings) into filled disks. It takes a polygon layer, dissolves by a specified field, splits into per-value layers, then iteratively unions and dissolves the layers in sorted order to fill holes, producing solid polygon disks. The output is a merged polygon layer with the original fields, after deleting an extraneous 'fid' column.

Russian doll polygon nesting. The script implements a Russian doll nesting algorithm for vector polygon layers. It takes a polygon layer and a field, sorts the polygons by that field, and then either unions or intersects them sequentially to create a nested arrangement where each polygon is contained within the previous one. Optionally, it can apply a buffer distance for inset/outset and snap geometries. If the ring option is enabled, it cuts out the inner polygon from the outer to produce distinct annular rings. Finally, it merges the resulting geometries into a single output layer and optionally outputs the overall footprint (the outermost polygon).

Spatialize flood heights onto DTM. The script interpolates a vector layer containing spatial data of highest water levels (CPHE) and projects them onto a Digital Terrain Model (DTM) if provided. It supports multiple interpolation methods: bilinear, bicubic, rst (r.fillnulls), and stair-step (Voronoi polygons). Inputs include vector data (points or polygons), a numeric field for CPHE values, a minimum height, optional DTM, buffer distance, and an optional mask for zonal processing. Outputs are a raster of heights above the minimum height and a raster of the CPHE values.

Interpolate highest water level points. The script interpolates vector data containing Cotes des Plus Hautes Eau (CPHE) values into a raster surface using either stepwise Voronoi (escarpment) or r.fillnulls (bilinear, bicubic, rst) interpolation methods. Optionally, if a digital terrain model (MNT) is provided, it projects the interpolated CPHE onto the terrain to compute water heights above a minimum threshold, producing a flood height raster. Outputs include the CPHE raster and the height difference raster.

Create Base Point from Geographic Extent. The script generates a base point layer by creating a polygon from a hardcoded geographic extent in WGS84, applying a placeholder extraction expression (id=99), extracting the polygon vertices, and refactoring fields to output a point layer in GPKG format. It is part of the Mavic 3 Enterprise group for drone mission planning.

Create mapping flight plan polygon. The script generates a flight plan polygon by reprojecting an area plot and base point to EPSG:31981, buffering the plot and the shortest connecting line by 30 meters, merging them, and dissolving into a single KML output for UgCS drone flight software.

Generate canopy survey grid. The script reprojects an input polygon layer to EPSG:31981, applies a 250-meter buffer, creates a regular grid (hexagon, rectangle, or diamond) with user-specified cell width, and adds an ID field to the grid cells.

Generate drone route for canopy zoom photos. The script generates a UgCS-compatible JSON drone mission file for each hexagon cluster from a point layer of optimized canopy photography locations. It reads the point layer and a base point, processes them by hexagon and group, and creates waypoint segments with camera actions (dual capture at wide and zoom, then approach altitude zoom photo, then flight altitude waypoint) for each group of three points. Coordinate conversions are applied to fit the UgCS system. The output JSON files are saved to a specified folder, enabling automated drone flight for canopy zoom photography using a DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise.

Merge vector layers with field cleanup. The script merges multiple selected vector layers into a single output layer using QGIS native merge algorithm. It first reprojects layers to a target CRS if necessary, then merges them, and optionally removes the 'layer' and 'path' fields that are automatically added by the merge process. The output is a merged vector file with the specified coordinate reference system.

Count cable overlaps on infrastructure. The script counts the number of cable (CAVI) features that spatially overlap with each infrastructure line (INFRASTRUTTURA). It assigns unique IDs to both layers, applies a tiny buffer (1e-07 degrees) to cables to handle touch intersections, repairs and explodes infrastructure lines, then performs a spatial join with predicates 'contains', 'are within', and 'overlaps' to associate cable IDs. An aggregation step concatenates distinct cable IDs per infrastructure segment and computes the total count of overlaps. The output is the infrastructure layer with fields id_infr, concatenated cable IDs, and n_overlaps.

Multi-function vector processing toolbox. The script provides a multi-function toolbox for QGIS that includes several vector processing algorithms: batch merging of layers with optional field removal, batch reprojection to a target CRS, counting overlapping line features, extracting duplicate geometries, and transposing attribute tables to CSV. The tools use QGIS processing frameworks and allow user-selected layers, selected features, output paths, and CRS settings. Results are loaded into the QGIS project or saved as files.

Generate Fill Polygons. The QGIS processing algorithm generates fill polygons in empty regions bounded by a frame and linear/polygonal delimiters. It prepares and merges input layers, polygonizes the linear network, filters candidate polygons within the frame's unary union, outside existing areas, and above a minimum area threshold. The output is a polygon layer with 'id' and 'area_otf' fields.

Identify shiftable parking spaces. The plugin identifies street-side parking spaces that can be shifted into selected public parking garages based on available capacity and network distance. It computes service areas from parking garages along a street network within a user-defined radius, selects intersecting public parking spaces, evaluates capacity constraints including current utilization, target utilization, and restriction types (disabled, short-term, residential, etc.), and classifies parking spaces as fully, partially, or not shiftable. Outputs include a styled layer of parking garages with new utilization, a layer of parking spaces colored by shiftability category, and optionally CSV exports of results.

Biologically active surface classification from LiDAR. The script classifies terrain into biologically active (PBC) and non-active surfaces using a pre-trained Random Forest model applied to LiDAR point cloud data aggregated into hexagonal grids. It loads point cloud layers with attributes Red, Green, Blue, Z, Intensity, ReturnNumber, NumberOfReturns; clips points to a mask buffered by 1.5 m to preserve neighborhood geometry; aggregates points per hexagon and computes spectral and geometric features including chromaticity, vegetation indices, brightness, coefficient of variation, and neighborhood statistics (planarity, std_Z, std_I, std_brightness, I_contrast). The model predicts class probabilities for 14 land cover classes, sums probabilities of PBC classes (e.g., grass, ruderal, farmland, dirt road), and applies a threshold of 0.65 to determine final binary PBC label. Outputs include hexagon polygon layers with detailed predictions and confidence, styled QGIS layers, and CSV files for each mask area.

Extract building heights and roof slopes. The script extracts building heights and roof slopes from classified airborne LiDAR point clouds. It buffers building polygons, clips ground (Classification_2) and roof (Classification_6) point layers, assigns building and parcel IDs via spatial joins, and then uses DBSCAN segmentation and RANSAC plane fitting to compute roof slopes. For heights, it interpolates a ground surface, subtracts point-wise to get building heights, filters out superstructure outliers (chimneys/antennas), and determines ridge height. Results are written to the building layer, and the roof points are styled with a graduated turbo color ramp.

Calculate urban planning indicators for investment land parcels. The script computes urban planning indicators (building coverage, gross floor area, floor area ratio, biologically active area) for investment land parcels. It first processes predicted PPNZ points (with label=1) by buffering and aggregating to compute PPNZ area per parcel, then integrates building data to calculate building-related metrics, and finally derives indicators such as WPZ (building coverage ratio) and WPBC (biologically active area ratio). The outputs include an aggregated buffer layer and a styled parcel layer with all computed indicators.

Create GTFS shapes from OSM. The script creates GTFS shapes by assigning shape IDs to trips based on OSM road/rail networks. It downloads OSM ways (roads, railways, ferries) for a given extent, processes GTFS stop times to determine trip sequences, matches GTFS stops to OSM nodes using spatial joins and nearest neighbor operations, and generates routing networks with speed attributes. The output includes updated trips.txt with shape_id assignments and intermediate layer files for visualization and further processing.

Generate GTFS shapes using OSM routing. The script generates GTFS trip shapes by computing shortest paths on multimodal OSM networks (roads, tram, heavy rail, funicular, ferry) between consecutive stops for each line and trip. It preprocesses OSM stops, snaps off-road stops to the nearest road, creates mini-trips between stop pairs using QGIS shortest path algorithms, merges mini-trips into full trips, and calculates cumulative shape distances. Final outputs are trip shape geometries (GPKG) and CSV summaries with stop sequences and traveled distances.

Classify directional slope into polygons. The script computes directional slope (toward a user-specified azimuth) and perpendicular slope from a DEM using numpy gradient, keeps pixels where absolute perpendicular slope falls within given limits, bins directional slope into classes with a specified half-width, polygonizes the classified raster, optionally simplifies and filters polygons by area, and thins vertices. The output is a vector layer with slope class polygons and an attribute 'slope_deg'.

Identify Disconnected Poles and Chambers. The script performs quality control on utility network vector layers. It first fixes geometries of the 'route' line layer, then extracts 'poles' points that are spatially disjoint (not intersecting or touching) from the fixed routes, storing the result as a layer named 'Diconnected_Poles'. Similarly, it extracts 'chambers' points that are disjoint from the routes, but using an intermediate touch-based selection to refine the disconnected chambers, outputting a layer named 'Disconnected_Chambers'. Both output layers are added to the QGIS project for inspection.

Stream network extraction from DTM. The script extracts a stream network from a digital terrain model (DTM) by first filling sinks using the Wang & Liu algorithm (native:fillsinkswangliu), then computing flow accumulation and delineating streams with GRASS r.watershed (including optional drainage directions, half basins, and topographic index), converting the raster streams to vector lines via r.to.vect, and finally smoothing the vector geometry. Outputs include a filled DTM, raw and smoothed vector stream networks, and optional rasters for stream, drainage, half basins, and ln(a/tan(b)).

QGIS workflow: Vector spatial analysis, Buffer Analysis. This workflow contains 6 core geospatial operations, including Vector spatial analysis, Buffer Analysis, Image Masking. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

Bathymetric Preprocessing Feature Generation. The script preprocesses satellite imagery for bathymetric inversion by generating water masks (via polygon vector, Otsu NDWI, manual NDWI threshold, or 3-index NDWI/MNDWI/NWI), performing sunglint correction using the Hedley method on coastal, blue, green, and red bands, and computing a multi-band feature stack that includes raw bands, log-transformed bands, band ratios, and custom band math. It also applies deep water / optically shallow water (OSW) masking based on manual ROI or automatic NIR percentile thresholding, with optional median filtering, hole filling, and polygon extraction. Outputs are a land/water mask, sunglint-corrected image, feature stack, intermediate review bands, deep water threshold statistics CSV, and OSW mask and polygon.

Depth Map Cleaning and Slope Filtering. The script provides functions to preprocess bathymetric depth rasters. It removes positive pixel values (>=0) by setting them to a nodata value, eliminating likely land or shallow artifacts. The clean_depth_map function clamps depth values beyond a 1.5× max_depth threshold using a mask from a feature stack raster, removing deep anomalies and edge noise. The slope_filter_depth function computes slope in degrees and masks depth pixels where slope exceeds a given threshold, filtering out steep erroneous features. The outputs are filtered depth rasters ready for further bathymetric analysis.

Create Voronoi diagram from points. The script creates a Voronoi diagram from all points in a selected QGIS point layer. It first determines the boundary either from a user-chosen polygon layer that contains all points or by creating a convex hull of the points and adding a buffer. The QGIS processing algorithm 'qgis:voronoipolygons' generates the Voronoi polygons, which are then clipped to the boundary using 'native:clip'. The resulting polygon layer includes attributes such as point ID, area, source layer name, and creation timestamp.

Download Sentinel-2 land cover data. The script provides QGIS processing algorithms to download Sentinel-2 land cover data from Esri's Living Atlas for a user-specified year (2017-2025). For latitude/longitude or point input, it creates a point, reprojects to Web Mercator, buffers to generate an area of interest (AOI), then calls a pipeline to download, mosaic, and clip the land cover raster. For AOI input, it reprojects the AOI to the same CRS and downloads directly. Outputs include a clipped land cover raster and optionally an AOI polygon layer, with QML styles applied for visualization.

Building Evacuation Time Estimation. The script computes shortest walking evacuation routes and travel times for buildings within a flood zone to designated safe shelters. It uses OpenStreetMap road network data, optionally a digital elevation model for terrain-adjusted travel time using Tobler's hiking function. Buildings at risk are identified by intersecting building polygon layer with flood extent. Outputs include a building layer with assigned shelter and travel time, and an evacuation route line layer.

Create Valley Boundary. This algorithm creates a valley boundary line layer by subtracting valley floor polygons from intersecting microsheds polygons, converting the difference polygons to lines, applying smoothing, and dissolving to produce final valley boundary lines.

Generate microsheds from DEM. The script runs GRASS r.watershed on an input DEM with a user-defined threshold to delineate uniquely labeled watershed basins (microsheds). Optionally, it polygonizes the resulting basins raster using GDAL to produce a vector polygon layer of microsheds.

Delineate Valley Floor Using Cost Distance. The script delineates valley bottoms using a cost-distance approach. It takes a river network vector layer and a DEM raster layer as inputs. It computes slope from the DEM, conditions it, rasterizes the river, and runs GRASS r.cost to generate a cumulative cost surface from the river network. An initial cost distance threshold creates a coarse mask, within which the mean cost is computed and used to refine the mask. The refined mask is then polygonized, and polygons are cleaned by deleting holes, smoothing, and buffering to close narrow gaps. The final output is a valley floor polygon layer.

Export vector layers to file. The script provides a QGIS plugin dialog for batch exporting vector layers to various formats such as GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoPackage, CSV, Excel, KML, GML, FlatGeobuf, MapInfo TAB, SQLite, and DXF. Users select layers from the project, choose output format and CRS, specify a directory, and the tool exports each layer using QGIS processing or QgsVectorFileWriter with progress feedback and logging.

Convert land cover to Manning roughness. The script extracts Manning's n roughness coefficient for HEC-RAS hydraulic modeling from SIOSE land cover data. It reads a CSV mapping from SIOSE land cover codes (ID_COBERTURA_MAX) to Manning values, clips the SIOSE polygon layer to a user-defined area of interest, assigns Manning values based on the mapping, optionally dissolves polygons by Manning value, calculates polygon areas, and applies stable symbolization. Outputs a new vector layer with Manning values added.

Analyze hourly traffic congestion from Google Traffic tiles. The script extracts Google Traffic XYZ tiles for user-specified days and hours, clips them to a boundary polygon, and exports GeoTIFF rasters. Using HSV color thresholds on the RGB tile data, it classifies traffic congestion into four levels (Free flow, Moderate, Heavy, Severe) and computes a weighted congestion index raster. It generates hourly statistics, animated GIFs/MP4s with time labels and metrics overlays, and summary plots (stacked bar and mean congestion line charts). The processed outputs include hourly traffic GeoTIFFs, classified congestion rasters, index rasters, CSV tables, and optional animated visualizations.

Scale Sentinel-2 L2A to 10m reflectance. The script processes Sentinel-2 Level-2A (L2A) bottom-of-atmosphere reflectance products. It locates the IMG_DATA folder within the product directory, identifies the R10m, R20m, and R60m subdirectories, selects specific spectral bands (B01–B08, B11, B12), applies the standard scaling factor (0.0001) to convert digital numbers to surface reflectance, resamples bands with native resolution of 20m or 60m to 10m using nearest neighbour resampling, and merges all bands into a single 10m multiband GeoTIFF raster. The output bands are named (Aerosol, Blue, Green, Red, Red_Edge1–3, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2).

Fault Spine Extraction from Earthquakes. The script extracts fault spines from earthquake point catalogs by applying magnitude filtering, DBSCAN clustering, and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to each cluster. It generates a line vector layer representing smoothed fault orientations, including attributes such as average magnitude, strike angle, and length. The output is saved as a GeoPackage file and loaded into the QGIS project.

Urban facility network location optimization. This script optimizes urban facility locations using network-based accessibility analysis. It processes a road network (with optional cleaning), a population raster to create demand grid centroids, and optional point of interest layers for attractiveness weighting. It builds a weighted graph, computes network service distances within a service radius, and performs facility audit of existing facilities (if provided) with status classification. For optimization, it either runs maximum coverage location problem (MCLP) greedy to achieve a target coverage or P-median heuristic with swap search to select new facility locations. Equity diagnostics include Gini coefficient and Theil index. Outputs include new facilities, demand points with before-after metrics, existing facility audit, combined facilities, CSV/TXT reports, and multiple PNG charts (histograms, bar chart, scatter, Lorenz curve, before-after comparison).

Reproject TransCAD Israel Layer. The script fixes the coordinate reference system (CRS) of a vector layer that has coordinates in the TransCAD Israel TM projection but no assigned CRS. It first assigns the custom TransCAD CRS (get_transcad_crs()) without transforming the coordinates, then reprojects the layer to EPSG:4326, and finally reprojects to EPSG:2039 (Israel TM Grid). The output is a layer with the corrected projection.

Transit stop location optimization. The script optimizes transit stop locations by building a road network graph, aggregating population raster to grid cells to compute demand, and incorporating POI attractiveness. Candidate stops are generated from road vertices or corridor lines, then filtered by minimum Euclidean spacing. Two optimization models are provided: greedy MCLP to reach a target population coverage within a walk radius, and P-median heuristic to minimize population-weighted network distance for a fixed number of stops. The workflow includes optional network cleaning for topology, regulatory spacing compliance (simple or advanced corridor with variable spacing based on local demand intensity), and AI demand smoothing via RandomForest. Outputs include selected stop points, demand points with access distance and coverage attributes, CSV/TXT summary reports with coverage and equity metrics (Gini, Theil), and an access distance histogram PNG.

Indicative traffic assignment with UE. The script performs indicative traffic assignment without OD survey data. It generates synthetic origin-destination demand using a gravity model (with population raster and/or POI counts as mass, or zone area as fallback) inside a user-defined boundary. The road network is optionally auto-split at intersections, filtered by road class, and free-flow travel times and capacities are derived from fields or class defaults. Flows are assigned via All-or-Nothing (AoN) or Path-Size Logit (PSL) multi-path assignment. If User Equilibrium (UE) is enabled, the BPR congestion function updates link costs iteratively with MSA smoothing until convergence. Outputs: edge layer with assigned flow, travel time, volume/capacity ratio, and delay; zone polygon layer with origin/destination mass, generation/attraction, snapped node, and snap distance; OD desire lines; and optional CSVs for synthetic OD matrix and iteration log.

Analyze overlap of single polygon with multiple layers. The script performs a spatial overlap analysis for the first polygon of a property layer against multiple input polygon layers. It uses the QGIS processing toolbox to extract intersecting features, fix geometries, compute geometric intersections, and calculate overlapping areas. For each analysis layer, it produces an area report (total overlap area and percentage) and a layer of intersection polygons that retains all original attributes from the overlaying layers. Outputs are a report table (no geometry) and an intersection geometry layer.

Calculate traffic emission line sources. The script processes OSM road lines and trajectory data to generate traffic emission line sources for ENVI-met. It filters OSM road classes, splits lines by length, counts unique trajectory IDs within a search radius per hour for each segment, merges adjacent segments with similar hourly patterns using a tolerance, applies a user-defined scaling factor, and computes hourly emissions of NO, NO2, PM10, and PM2.5 using provided emission factors and NO/PM ratios. The outputs are a GeoPackage containing the merged segments with hourly traffic volumes and an ENVI-met JSON database (.edb) file ready for microclimate simulation.
