InSAR East-West and Up-Down decomposition. The script decomposes InSAR Line-of-Sight (LOS) velocities into East-West and Up-Down components using ascending and descending persistent scatterer (PS) point data. It aggregates PS point velocities into a regular grid by computing mean and count per cell, then applies geometric formulas based on satellite incidence and azimuth angles (right-looking convention) to derive horizontal and vertical motion components. Additional derived fields include total velocity magnitude, movement azimuth, and a classification flag (stable, up, down, east, west). Outputs are polygon and centroid vector layers containing the decomposed fields.

Generate clipped grid over polygon. The script generates a grid (points, lines, or rectangles) over an input polygon vector layer. It first uses the QGIS native:creategrid processing algorithm to create a grid covering the input layer’s extent with user-defined horizontal and vertical spacing and grid type. Then it extracts only the grid features that intersect the input polygon using native:extractbylocation, producing a clipped grid layer. User preferences (spacing, grid type, verbose logging) are saved for the next run.

Calculate line center points. The script processes a line feature layer by fixing geometries, reprojecting to a chosen CRS, and then using geometry by expression to compute the centroid of the line substring from the midpoint to the start of each line, generating a point layer of those centroids.

QGIS workflow: Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Projection. This workflow contains 64 core geospatial operations, including Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Projection, Vector spatial analysis, Vector data attribute editing. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

Polygonize Outer Road Lines and Join to Zones. The script filters a UIP line layer to extract outer road boundaries (where 'side' attribute contains 'outer'), polygonizes them to create road polygons, then performs a spatial join by location to assign attributes from a reference UIP zone polygon layer based on the largest overlap, producing a final road polygon layer with zone attributes.

Segment road frontage and assign coefficients. The script processes road boundary lines from a master plan to segment them into 10-meter segments and assign road-type-based coefficients and frontage types. It first filters features where the side attribute is 'left_outer' or 'right_outer', then splits the resulting lines into 10-meter segments. For each segment, it maps the road type (yolTipi) to a coefficient value (e.g., motorway=2.5, divided road=1.6, road=1.0, pedestrian=0.4) and validates the frontage type from the 'type' field against a predefined list, then writes the output with added 'katsayi' and 'cephe_tipi' fields.

Remove black border from raster. The script removes dark/black borders from georeferenced raster images. It reads the input raster, applies a threshold to detect pixels above a certain value (indicating valid image content), generates a mask, optionally applies morphological closing to preserve valid dark interior features, vectorizes the mask into a polygon, and clips the raster to that polygon, removing the black border. The output is a new GeoTIFF file with the border removed, and optionally with an alpha channel for transparency.

Parcel subdivision from building blocks. The script subdivides input polygon features representing building blocks into individual parcels with configurable parameters including target parcel width, width variation, row asymmetry, and fishbone offsets. It processes irregular polygons using oriented minimum bounding boxes, generates division lines along the short axis, and applies width variations and optional asymmetric splitting to create varied parcel sizes. A three-pass merging step removes small fragments below a user-defined threshold. Outputs include parcels with attributes for area, facade information, and unique parcel IDs.

API load accumulation in rivers. The script accumulates pharmaceutical loads (APIs) along a river network to compute concentrations under mean and low flow conditions. It takes emission load points and a river network (lines or polygons), splits lines at emission points, accumulates loads downstream using a routing topology defined by NET_ID/NET_TO fields, and calculates concentrations (ng/L) based on accumulated flow (m³/s). It optionally processes monitoring points to extract modeled concentrations and computes dilution ratios using wastewater treatment plant effluent (Q_WWTP). The output includes an accumulated river network layer, monitoring point results, and a dilution ratio layer.

Optimize agricultural plot layout. The script designs optimized agricultural unit layouts (strips or mosaics) for a given parcel, using geometric primitives arranged in rows or Hilbert curve patterns. It calculates cultivated area, aisle area, efficiency, and discards small fragments below a threshold. Outputs include vector layers (Layout_Strips, Layout_Mosaics, GPS_Guide_Lines, Hilbert_Path, Unit_Centers, Labels_Mosaics, Labels_Strips, Coord_Layer), labeled centers, coordinate labels, and terminal reports with area and efficiency statistics.

Prepare Open Geospatial Enrichment Data. The script prepares OSM roads and facilities, WorldPop population rasters, Copernicus DEM elevation/slope/ruggedness, and ESA WorldCover land cover for a user-defined area of interest (AOI) in QGIS. It downloads data from Overpass API, WorldPop, Copernicus DEM COG, and ESA WorldCover S3, clips or merges rasters to the AOI bounding box, caches data, and writes GeoPackage (vector) and GeoTIFF (raster) outputs along with a manifest file for tracking.

Clip vector layers to DWG. The script clips visible vector layers in QGIS to a user-defined bounding box and exports the result as a DWG file. It first captures a box drawn on the map canvas, then clips each layer using QGIS processing algorithm 'native:clip', handles polygon boundary lines separately for accurate representation, applies symbology, writes a temporary DXF with QgsDxfExport, post-processes the DXF to remove invisible hatch entities and force ByLayer attributes, and finally invokes the ODA File Converter in a background task to convert the DXF to DWG.

Allocate origin-destination flows on Delaunay network. The script performs All-or-Nothing (AoN) traffic allocation over a Delaunay triangulation network built from input centroids. It creates the network by triangulating centroids, extracting unique edges, and constructing a graph with edge lengths as cost. For each origin-destination pair, it runs Dijkstra shortest-path routing and loads the entire flow onto the least-cost path. The output is a line layer with total flow per edge and optional directional volumes (flow_ab, flow_ba).

Vectorize Raster Values into Polygons. The plugin processes a raster layer to generate polygon vector layers based on user-defined unique values or ranges. It first optionally clips the raster to a mask extent, reclassifies the raster to a binary mask per value/range, polygonizes the reclassified raster, clips the resulting vectors with a mask layer if provided, joins attribute tables with labels, and calculates areas in m² and ha. Outputs vector layers are added to the QGIS project.

QGIS workflow: Vector spatial analysis, Projection. This workflow contains 20 core geospatial operations, including Vector spatial analysis, Projection, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Data import. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

Waterbody extraction from multispectral indices. The script extracts waterbodies from multispectral satellite imagery using a decision-tree based on NDVI, MNDWI, and NWI water indices. It computes these indices from user-specified bands (Blue, Green, Red, NIR, SWIR), applies a raster mask formula (MNDWI>0 AND NWI>0 AND NDVI<0.1), performs raster noise removal via sieve filtering, polygonizes the mask, extracts water features, and optionally smooths vector edges. Outputs include the three index rasters, the final binary water mask raster, and a smoothed waterbody polygon, all reprojected to EPSG:4326.

Calculate Water Utilization Capability Index. The script calculates the Water Utilization Capability Index (IKP Air) for grid cells by integrating water supply, water quality, and water demand components. It first computes water availability per grid by intersecting a water provisioning index layer (JLH) with river basin boundaries (WS), distributing basin-level water supply proportionally based on a water service indicator (ije_pa). It then joins a pollution index table (Indeks Pencemar) to calculate contaminated and usable water. Population and land-use layers are joined to derive total water demand, combining land-based demand (using land class weights and area) and population-based demand (43.2 m³/year per capita doubled). The final IKP is computed as total demand divided by usable water, classified into five capability classes (Sangat Tinggi to Sangat Rendah), and assigned scores 1–5. Outputs include a polygon layer with fields IKPAIR, KIKPAIR, SIKPAIR, air_ws, air_layak, demand components, and auxiliary indicators.

Compute Air Utilization Capability Index. The script calculates the Air Utilization Capability Index (IKP Udara) by integrating PM2.5 concentration (from raster), climate projection (IPS vector with SKOR), and land carrying capacity (PKU year-based grid) to generate a per-polygon and per-grid index, including classification into five levels. It processes PM2.5 raster reclassification, calculates IP and IKU indices, interpolates IKU using IDW, performs zonal statistics, and intersects layers to compute the final IKP Udara index, classified into 'Sangat Rendah' to 'Sangat Tinggi'.

Calculate D3TLH Composite Index. This script integrates multiple environmental carrying capacity indices (IKP Air, IKP Udara, IKP Lahan, IKP Kehati) and an environmental behavior index (IPRLH) into a single composite D3TLH index. It sequentially joins the input grids using a common ID field, computes a weighted average of the normalized scores for the four IKP components, classifies them into qualitative categories (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi), assigns quantitative scores, joins the IPRLH table by province, and then calculates the final D3TLH as the average of the integrated IKP score and the IPRLH. The output is a vector layer with the D3TLH field, designed for environmental planning and monitoring in Indonesia.

Calculate habitat biodiversity ecosystem index. Calculates the Habitat and Biodiversity Supporting Ecosystem Service Index (IJLH_PHK) using land cover, ecoregion, and special criteria layers. The workflow intersects land cover with ecoregion, joins scoring tables for Keanekaragaman Bentang Alam (KBA), Keanekaragaman Vegetasi (KVA), and land cover (PL), computes a weighted index (weights: ecoregion 0.24, vegetation 0.16, land cover 0.60), applies overrides for special criteria (e.g., designated conservation areas, savanna in certain provinces, water bodies), and generates either a polygon or grid output with categorized index (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi). Supports national or island-specific scoring modes.

Calculate Air Quality Regulation Index. The script calculates the Air Quality Regulation ecosystem service index (JLH_PKU) from land cover and ecoregion data based on D3TLH 2024 guidelines. It intersects the land cover and ecoregion layers, joins scoring tables for ecoregion (KBA), vegetation (KVA), and land cover (PL), computes a weighted sum (0.15*S_EK + 0.25*S_VE + 0.60*S_PL) to produce the index, and optionally aggregates to a grid by area-weighted averaging. The output includes the index value and a categorical classification (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi).

Calculate water regulation ecosystem service index. The script computes the Flood Regulation Ecosystem Service Index (JLH_PGA) based on land cover, ecoregion, and scoring tables from the D3TLH guidelines. It processes user-provided vector layers: Penutup Lahan (land cover) and Ekoregion (ecoregion). The workflow includes intersecting land cover with ecoregion, joining scoring CSVs for KBA, KVA, and Land Cover (either national or island-specific), and calculating a weighted sum (0.28*S_EK + 0.12*S_VE + 0.60*S_PL). Special criteria reassign a score of 5 for water body types. The resulting index is categorized into five classes (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi). Output can be polygon (preserving original geometry) or grid (with proportional aggregation and dominant land cover via MCA). The final output is a vector layer with standardized field names and the index categories.

Map water provision ecosystem service index. This QGIS processing algorithm calculates the Water Provision Ecosystem Service Index (JLH_PYA) by spatially intersecting land cover and ecoregion layers, joining attribute scores from CSV lookup tables for ecoregion (S_EK), vegetation (S_VE), and land cover (S_PL), then computing the weighted sum (0.32*S_EK + 0.08*S_VE + 0.60*S_PL). It outputs polygon or grid features with the index and categorical classification (Very Low to Very High). For kabupaten/kota analysis, water body classes are automatically assigned a perfect score of 5.

Calculate Food Provision Ecosystem Service Index. The script computes the Food Provision Ecosystem Service Index (JLH_PGN) by intersecting land cover with ecoregion, joining ecological scores (KBA, KVA) from CSV tables, joining land-cover scores specific to each Indonesian island, and calculating a weighted sum using fixed coefficients (0.28, 0.12, 0.60). It can output the index as polygons or aggregate it into a user-supplied grid using area-weighting, and classifies the index into five qualitative categories (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi). The final output includes standardized fields for the index and category.

Calculate Carbon Sequestration-Storage Index. This algorithm calculates the Carbon Sequestration and Storage Ecosystem Service Index (JLH PPK) by intersecting land cover and ecoregion vector layers, joining scoring tables for ecoregion (KBA_250), vegetation (KVA_250), and land cover (PL) based on national or Kabupaten/Kota settings, then applying a weighted formula (0.20 ecoregion + 0.20 vegetation + 0.60 land cover). The output can be polygonal or gridded; when gridded, values are proportionally weighted by area within each grid cell. The result includes a numeric index and a categorical classification (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi).

Generate SGSRI grid with administrative attributes. The script generates a hierarchical square-cell grid based on the Indonesian Multi-scale Grid System (SGSRI), using a specified spatial extent and grid size. It assigns unique grid IDs based on cell coordinates relative to the SGSRI origin (90°E, 15°S). Then, it enriches each grid cell with administrative region attributes (Desa/Kelurahan, Kecamatan, Kabupaten/Kota, Provinsi) by intersecting with an input administrative boundary layer and applying a maximum coverage area rule. Optionally, it clips the output grid to the input boundary. Output is a polygon vector layer with fields: ID, WADMKD, WADMKC, WADMKK, WADMPR.

Calculate dominant attribute per grid by MCA. The script calculates the dominant attribute from a secondary polygon layer for each polygon in a grid layer based on the largest combined area of intersection (MCA method). It performs intersection, dissolve by ID and attribute, area calculation in EPSG:3857, finds maximum area per grid cell, and joins the dominant class back to the original grid. Output is a grid vector layer with a new column of the dominant attribute.

Calculate urban morphology metrics. The script calculates urban morphology indicators (footprint ratio, floor area ratio, building volume, and building height standard deviation) for two sets of spatial units (SA1 and SA2) using building footprint geometry and height attributes. It loads unit and building layers, reprojects to EPSG:7856, computes unit grid area, intersects buildings with units, calculates per-unit building area sum and volume sum, then derives FP (total building footprint area / grid area), FAR (total building volume / grid area), V (mean building volume), and AHSD (standard deviation of building heights). Results are written back to output shapefiles after removing temporary unique ID fields.

Zonal mean calculation for remote sensing indices. The script computes zonal mean values of multiple remote sensing indices (EVI, LST, NDBSI, Tasseled Cap Wetness, and three white-sky albedo components: nir, shortwave, vis) within statistical area polygons (SA2 for training, SA1 for prediction). It first reprojects the zone shapefiles to EPSG:7856, fixes any invalid geometries, then iterates over the raster files, warping each to the same CRS. Using QGIS native zonal statistics, it calculates the pixel mean of each raster band within each polygon, renames the output fields to meaningful index names (EVI, LST, NDBSI, WET, nir, shortwave, vis), and saves the enriched shapefiles (SA2_remote.shp, SA1_remote.shp) to the preprocessing intermediate folder, adding them as map layers in QGIS.

Calculate urban building morphology indicators. The script calculates urban morphology indicators (FP, FAR, V, AHSD) for two statistical area layers (SA1 and SA2) using building footprint data. It reprojects both unit and building layers to EPSG:7856 for accurate area and volume computations, performs an intersection to associate building footprints with units, then for each unit computes footprint ratio (FP = total building area / unit area), floor area ratio (FAR = total building volume / unit area), mean building volume (V), and standard deviation of building heights (AHSD). The resulting indicators are written as new shapefiles (SA1_morphology.shp and SA2_morphology.shp) and added to the QGIS project.

Extract zonal means of remote sensing indices. The script reprojects SA2 and SA1 shapefiles to EPSG:7856, then for each remote sensing raster (EVI, LST, NDBSI, WET, nir, shortwave, vis) in the training and prediction folders, it warps the raster to the same CRS, computes zonal statistics (mean) for each polygon, renames fields to corresponding index names, and saves the enriched shapefiles as SA2_remote.shp and SA1_remote.shp.
